articleTitle: Impact of Overhead Grounding Wire Arrangement on Induced Voltage of Adjacent Pipelines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Transmission lines have the electromagnetic interference effects on adjacent buried pipelines, which is not benefit to the pipeline safety. This paper researches the impact of overhead grounding wire arrangement modes on the electromagnetic interference during a short-circuit fault occurs on the transmission line. The overhead transmission lines usually have two ground wires. These two ground wires can be both grounded at each tower or can be both segment-insulated with a single grounded point. In addition, one ground wire can be grounded at each tower, and the other one ground wire can be segment-insulated with a single grounded point. The induced voltage of pipeline and the power loss of transmission line are analyzed when the overhead grounding wires adopt different arrangement modes. Through extensive CDEGS simulations and analysis, the impact of overhead grounding wire arrangement are revealed in this paper. When the overhead grounding wires are both grounded at each tower, the adjacent pipeline has the smallest induced voltage, while the transmission line have the largest power loss. When the overhead grounding wires are both segment-insulated with a single grounded point, the adjacent pipeline has the largest induced voltage, while the transmission line have the smallest power loss. Furthermore, with the increase of the number of grounding points in each segment, although the power loss in the overhead grounding wires increases, the induced voltage of nearby pipelines decreases. These above results are useful for the design of transmission line arrangements and the protection of buried pipelines.

articleTitle: A Single-Phase to Ground Fault Location Method Based on Last-Squares Parameter Estimation in Arc-Suppression-Coil Grounding System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The accuracy of the distribution network fault location is important to guarantee the safety and reliability of the power system. There are many achievements in the research of fault location technology for the distribution network, but it is still difficult to locate fault of neutral point via arc suppression coil grounding system accurately in the application of single-phase to ground fault line selection or detection, because of the problems of a lack of fault selection components, inaccurate line parameters and expensive phase angle information collection devices. This paper proposes a fault location method of single-phase to ground fault based on least-squares parameter estimation. Taking the zero-sequence equivalent circuit model of single-phase ground fault as the basis, regarding the fault distance, fault resistance and inaccurate line parameters as the unknow parameters, and treating the time domain relationship between the fault zero-sequence voltage and current reflected through the zero-sequence equivalent circuit as fault location equation, the optimum solution of the distance from the fault point to the busbar can be calculated with the least-square parameter estimation method. In addition, the method takes the unknown nature of the parameters into account, and only need to measure the fault three-phase voltage and three-phase current data for determining the fault location without phase angle information. The validity of the method was verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement for Pilot Protection of Double Circuit Lines on the Same Tower Based on Power Converse Accurate Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The power converse phenomenon, which frequently occurs on double circuit lines on the same tower, can cause the pilot protection of non-fault lines misoperation. Firstly the reasons for the occurrence of power converse and its influence on pilot protection are clarified. Then this paper presents a performance improvement scheme for pilot protection of double circuit lines on the same tower based on the fully using the substation-area information. The scheme consists of two parts, which are accurate identification method for power converse and determining method of blocking delay during power converse period. It identifies the power converse according to the different trips of circuit breakers on the faulted line and adjusts the blocking time of non-fault line in real time. A typical model of double circuit lines was established in PSCAD to verify the correctness of the proposed scheme and carried out a detailed comparison with existing methods. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme can accurately identify the occurrence of power reversal and strictly match the blocking time of the pilot protection with the time period of power converse. Therefore, the protection performance has been effectively improved.

Author Keywords: double circuit lines on the same tower

articleTitle: Fault Location Method for Distribution Lines Based on Coordination of Primary and Secondary Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: After a fault occurs in a distribution line, the fault transient information decays rapidly, the effective time window for transient information measuring and sampling is short. At the same time, the existence of timing errors between different measuring devices also affects the accuracy of the fault location. For this reason, this paper proposes a fault location method for distribution lines based on coordination of primary and secondary devices, provides steady-state fault information for fault location by putting in auxiliary inductors after tripping; for asymmetric short-circuit faults, the fault point voltage is solved based on the voltage and current at both end of the line, the ratio of the positive and negative sequence voltages are used to eliminate the asynchronous angle and obtain the fault location functions. For symmetrical short-circuit faults, the ratio of the voltage of the two fault phases are used to eliminate the asynchronous angle and obtain the fault location function. The simulation results show that the method has a high accuracy, not affected by the fault location, the transition resistance, the fault type and the asynchronous angle.

articleTitle: A Simulation-Based Method for Distribution Line Localized Protection Device Development
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: For protective relay vendors, traditionally, before evaluating the performance of new protection algorithms, it was necessary to develop the corresponding hardware and generate various electrical signals in different operating scenarios, such as voltage and current signals at protection terminals under fault conditions, through techniques including electromagnetic transient programs. This was done to test and improve protection algorithms and devices. This method was time-consuming, labor-intensive, costly, and constrained by testing equipment, such as protective relay test sets and real-time digital simulator, making it a cumbersome and inconvenient process. This paper proposes a simulation-based method for the development of protection devices, and is applied to the development of localized distribution line protection device development. This method simulates the localized protective relays deployed in distribution lines using software tools such as PSCAD, and then verifies and improves the accuracy of the software simulation model by comparing it with the performance of actual devices. Once the accuracy of the simulation model is validated, for the development of new protection principles, simulation based on the protection principles can be performed first, and then the electrical fault signals generated by electromagnetic transient simulation software can be used to verify and improve the new protection principles. With this method, there is no need to produce hardware in the early stages of developing new protection principles and devices when the principles are not yet mature. Instead, thorough accurate modeling, improvement and the formation of mature solutions can be accomplished, reducing device development costs and improving development efficiency.

articleTitle: Substation Transformer Abnormality Diagnosis Technology Based on Multi-Source Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The monitoring system and auxiliary control system of transformers in substations are currently independent of each other and the data are not accessible. A single platform cannot comprehensively diagnose the health status of transformers. This paper focuses on daily monitoring and fault diagnosis, and deeply integrates the remote signaling, remote measurement data and various online monitoring data of transformers to achieve precise load warning, oil temperature prediction, post-fault evaluation and other functions. By designing alarm trigger conditions, program jump logic and other links, the dynamic and comprehensive evaluation of transformer status is realized. The research of this technology provides a new idea for multi-source diagnosis of primary equipment in substations and effectively integrates the collected information in the station.

articleTitle: Abnormal Detection Method of High-Voltage Switchgear Cabinet in Power Distribution Room Based on SSD-MobileNet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of high risk coefficient, low efficiency and easy to make mistakes in the substation distribution room equipment depending on manual inspection, this paper proposes an anomaly detection method for high-voltage switchgear in the distribution room based on SSD-MobileNet. First of all, the collected image data of high-voltage switchgear is expanded through data enhancement technologies such as clipping and zooming to establish an anomaly detection data set. Then, an anomaly detection model of high-voltage switchgear based on SSD-MobileNet is constructed, and lightweight network MobileNet is introduced to replace the basic feature extraction network VGG16 in SSD, which improves the speed and accuracy of target detection of the model. Based on SSD-MobileNet algorithm, the depth feature extraction and mining of image data are carried out to achieve intelligent detection and identification of three types of abnormal conditions with high frequency in high-voltage switchgear. Finally, through case analysis and comparative experiments, it shows the effectiveness and accuracy of the method, which can assist the substation patrol inspectors to quickly locate and handle faults, and improve the substation management level and operation and maintenance efficiency.

articleTitle: A Strategy of Adaptive Reclosure for AC Lines on the Inverter Side of AC/DC Hybrid Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The electrical characteristics of the AC lines on the inverter-side of HVDC and AC system are comparatively analyzed when different types of faults occur. A three-phase adaptive reclosing criterion based on the differential current of the power frequency traveling wave is proposed. The method utilizes the voltage and the shunt reactor current to construct the power frequency traveling wave. After the three-phase tripping out at both ends of the transmission line, the phases of the power frequency line mode traveling wave differential current have different trends under different phase fault properties, in which the phase change period during permanent faults is much smaller than that during transient faults. By utilizing this characteristic, a three-phase adaptive reclosing criterion is proposed for the inverter-side AC line of HVDC. The criterion is calculated by using the traveling wave quantity of power frequency, which can quickly and accurately distinguish transient faults from permanent faults, and at the same time, it has excellent resistance to transition resistance.

articleTitle: Traveling Wave Differential Protection Applied to Renewable Energy and Flexible DC Connected Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the rapid consumption of non-renewable energy such as fossil energy, countries around the world are vigorously developing wind, light, geothermal and other renewable energy. Since most of the large-scale renewable energy power stations are located in remote areas, in order to better connect renewable energy to the grid, renewable energy is widely used through the flexible DC connection transmission scheme. The AC line of the renewable energy power station incorporated into the flexible DC double ended converter power supply has new fault characteristics. This paper introduces the application of traveling wave differential protection in this scenario, and uses Euclid distance to characterize the waveform similarity, and adopt normalization method to further optimize the protection performance and protection setting. Finally, the effectiveness of the protection algorithm is verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Single Phase Grounding Fault Line Selection Method of Resonant Grounding System Based on Recurrence Quantification Analysis and Fuzzy C-Means Clustering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The discrimination degree of the transient zero-sequence current of each line is reduced by the wide application of cable lines and the harmonic injection of a high proportion of new energy when a single phase grounding fault occurs in the distribution network. Aiming at this problem, a single phase grounding fault line selection method based on recurrence quantification analysis and fuzzy C-means clustering is proposed. Firstly, the transient zero-sequence current of the line with three different window lengths after the fault is collected, and the low-frequency component is extracted by FIR filter and the recurrence diagram is drawn. Secondly, the recurrence entropy of low-frequency transient zero-sequence current with different window lengths is calculated by recurrence quantification analysis, and a three-dimensional sample matrix is obtained. Finally, the fuzzy C-means clustering is used to classify the sample matrix to complete the fault line selection. The distribution network model is built using PSCAD to simulate the line selection conditions under different fault conditions such as grounding points, grounding resistance and fault angles, all of which can be correctly selected. The simulation results show that the proposed line selection method is not affected by the reduction of line transient zero-sequence current discrimination, and has strong noise immunity and high line selection accuracy.

Author Keywords: Single phase grounding fault line selection

articleTitle: Research on Voltage Detection Method of UPQC Based on NF-FLL
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Unified power quality controller, as a comprehensive power quality control equipment, can effectively control the power quality of distribution network. In order to solve the problem of frequency fluctuation and multiple zero crossing of voltage in traditional synchronous reference system of UPQC, UPQC integrated Photovoltaic-battery energy storage system (PV-BESS) can make comprehensive governance of power grid. The PV-BESS unit ensures uninterrupted power supply to the system under extreme conditions. Notch filter-based phase-locked loop (NF-PLL) based on notch filter was proposed, and an improved voltage detection method based on notch filter phase locked loop (NF-PLL) was proposed. The UPQC simulation platform was built, and the simulation verification was carried out under two conditions of three-phase voltage distortion and voltage sag. The simulation results showed that the proposed voltage detection method can detect and compensate the voltage sag effectively and quickly.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis and Comparative Study of Power Conversion System Main Topology Using SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Effective thermal management is crucial in the field of power converter design to ensure optimal performance and reliability of power devices. Power conversion system (PCS) is the key equipment for energy storage system in new power system. In this paper, the critical issue of thermal design of the PCS main topology for battery energy storage system is addressed. Failure to dissipate the heat properly can lead to increased temperature, and reduce component performance and lifespan, as well as reducing the efficiency of overall equipment. In this paper, losses of key power devices are calculated. Then, a simplified three-dimensional model of the designed compact structure of these components with printed circuit board (PCB) is established. By using the estimated losses of the power devices as temperature field heat sources, the thermal field of the designed structure is solved by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to validate the rationality of the design. Furthermore, the performance of using SiC MOSFETs and traditional IGBTs in terms of heat dissipation on the temperature field are compared and analyzed. The CFD results verify that the designed structure utilizing SiC MOSFETs achieves better heat dissipation performance.

articleTitle: An Internal Fault Model of a Transformer Bank Using the UDM of Matlab/Simulink
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: This paper aims to propose a UDM(User-Defined Model) for internal faults of a 154kV three-winding transformer using Matlab Simulink. The model is configured by Multi-Winding Transformer block provided by Simulink, and it can be used in various tests of the transformer protection relays more efficiently by modularizing the system blocks that simulate various transformer internal faults. The UDM proposed in the paper is a module consists of several blocks inside. To verify the validity of this module, an internal fault simulation was performed and the magnitude of the fault current was compared with the calculated value that was obtained from the theoretical fault calculation using positive and zero sequence impedance of the transformer. In addition, it is evaluated by comparing the transient states of the fault current of the same transformer system modeled by PSCAD/EMTDC under the same internal fault cases.

articleTitle: Adaptive Reclosing Strategy for Distribution Network Based on Three-Phase Additional Inductance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The traditional distribution network reclosing uses automatic reclosing, which is simple and efficient, but when reclosing on a permanent fault, the system will again generate short-circuit current, which will have a large impact on the system equipment. As the distribution network is used without shunt reactor and three-phase reclosing, it leads to the rapid decay of the line electrical quantity after the three-phase circuit breaker is tripped, which is not conducive to the determination of the nature of the fault. In view of the above problems, this paper proposes an adaptive reclosing strategy based on three-phase additional inductance, a three-phase inductor is incorporated on both sides of the circuit breaker at the exit of the bus, the three-phase inductors added during the normal line have no coupling effect on the line, and the fault currents are significantly higher than the current value of the transient faults in the case of permanent faults, so as to realize the judgment on the nature of the fault, and then realize the adaptive reclosing. The theoretical derivation and simulation verification based on PSCAD/EMTDC show that the proposed adaptive reclosing strategy is simple, accurate, reliable, and less affected by the transition resistance and fault location.

articleTitle: Review on Icing Fault Prediction for Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Icing, a phenomenon that occurs in extremely cold weather, poses significant challenges to the operation and reliability of overhead transmission line (OHTL). Consequently, drawing upon the comprehensive analysis of icing hazard, the primary objective of this paper is to provide a comprehensive overview of the existing research on fault prediction. Firstly, the paper encompasses historical icing accidents to grasp an understanding of the potential hazard that can lead to mechanical damage, electrical damage, and maintenance issues caused by icing. Secondly, according to the nonlinear relationship between the line fault risk and the ice wind load, the current research progress and technical difficulties of fault prediction are discussed in detail. Finally, this paper outlines the prospective future directions for predicting icing fault on OHTL. In the future, it is possible to quantitatively calculate the fault risk of icing and establish an emergency decision-making model for ice melting with the goal of minimizing the risk of power system, so as to provide decision-making guidance for efficient ice melting.

Author Keywords: comprehensive load of ice and wind

articleTitle: A Weak Fault Adaptive Traveling Wave Protection Method for Bus and Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the increasing number of ultrahigh-voltage transmission lines, the protection with ultrahigh speed is increasingly urgent. Traveling wave protection has the advantage of ultrahigh speed. But it has not yet been widely applied, because it has low reliability in the condition of weak faults, i.e. small initial fault angle and large transition resistance. The reliability of traveling wave protection is low because the initial fault angle and transition resistance have great influence on the transient quantity produced by the fault. This paper proposed a relay basing on the high-frequency fault current which was normalized by initial fault angle and transition resistance. The normalized fault high frequency current contains initial fault angle and transition resistance information. It removed the influence of fault angle and transition resistance by using the normalized high frequency current to construct the action criterion for fault judgment. It improved the algorithm's reliability. In this algorithm, the fault high frequency current and fault direction were used as joint criteria for fault judgment. The presented method protects a bus and a transmission line at the same time. It was verified using ATP/EMTP. Simulation results showed the algorithm reliably determined whether the fault was occurring in the line, or in the busbar, or outer side zone.

articleTitle: Comparison of Different Power Flow Models in Power System Cascading Outage Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Cascading outage is the most severe event for the power systems. Power flow model is an essential part in cascading outage simulation. In existing methods, traditional cascading outage simulation such as OPA model uses DC power flow. Despite simple, its effectiveness and limits are not fully discussed. In this paper, different power flow models, including the AC power flow model and DC power flow model, are applied and compared in cascading simulation. Particularly, the DC power flow model is embedded into the cascading simulation code in Matlab, while the AC power flow is carried out by BPA and Matlab. The simulation on IEEE-39 bus system verify the conclusion that these two power flow models have little impacts on the initial result of cascading outage simulation. However, AC power flow can reflect the power flow convergence problem as cascading outage develops.

articleTitle: Method for Determining the Minimum Capacity Scale of Generators Under Voltage Stability Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: As the proportion of power received by the receiving end of the power grid increases., the voltage characteristics of the power grid also deteriorate. To maintain the stability of the power grid voltage., requirements have been put forward for the minimum capacity scale of the generator units in the system. This paper proposes a calculation method for effectively evaluating the minimum capacity scale of generators under voltage stability constraints. In this technique., the proposed method is based on the node impedance matrix of system and the capacity of all synchronous machines to obtain the equivalent synchronous machine capacity of the weak points of voltage stability characteristics., then the equivalent impedance of the equivalent synchronous machine at that point can be obtained. By comparing the magnitude of the equivalent impedance with the self-impedance of that point., the voltage stability characteristics of that point are determined., and it is further known whether the system generator capacity meets the voltage stability constraint. Extensive simulation results of a system connected with a high proportion of DC indicate that the proposed calculation method can effectively evaluate the minimum capacity scale of the generators under voltage stability constraints.

articleTitle: A Pilot Protection Principle Based on the Structure Similarity of Transient Energy Waveform for Hybrid HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: To improve the ability of rapid fault clearing of hybrid multi-terminal High-voltage direct current transmission (HVDC) lines and ensure the safe operation of electric power transmission, a principle of hybrid HVDC system pilot protection based on the structure similarity for the of transient energy waveform is proposed. In this paper, the fault additional network diagrams of the S-domain under different fault conditions are analyzed, and it is found that there are differences in the transient power of the protection measurement points at both ends of the line during internal or external faults. On this basis, the time-domain transient power obtained by time-domain voltage and current convolution is used to characterize the S-domain power characteristics. Integrate the transient power in the time domain and obtain the transient energy waveform through a sliding window. Structural similarity is used to compare the similarity of transient energy waveforms at both ends of the transmission line, to identify internal and external faults and select fault poles. Simulation verification based on PSCAD/EMTDC shows that the proposed protection principle can reliably identify the fault area and fault pole in the case of 300 Ω fault resistance and 30dB noise interference. It is highly resistant to fault resistance and noise interference. Besides, it is not affected by transient processes and can achieve protection quickly.

articleTitle: Transient protection based on phase difference
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the increase of new energy penetration, the ne w electric power system will present ‘double high’ characteristics-high proportion of renewable energy and high proportion of pow er electronic equipment access, the power grid structure is more c omplex, the transient response speed is faster, and the response s peed of the first defense line of the power system is also put forwa rd higher requirements. The action time limit of the main power f requency protection of the traditional ultra-high voltage system is 15 to 20 milliseconds, and the main protection action time of the transient protection is 2 to 5 milliseconds, which meets the requir ements of the new power system for the protection speed. Firstly, the principle of wave process is analyzed from the perspective of I ine infinitesimal, and the propagation process of current travelin g wave in transmission line is introduced. The difference between line modulus and phase modulus after phase mode transformatio n is pointed out, and the rationality of phase mode channel is veri fied. Secondly, according to the principle of traveling wave trans mission, the process of refraction and reflection of traveling wave at bus bar is studied, which leads to the difference of phase of hig h frequency current in internal and external faults. Using FFT al gorithm to extract this feature, a new principle of transient prote ction based on phase difference is proposed. Finally, the simulatio n test is carried out in the flexible DC full electromagnetic transie nt model. The scheme has good applicability to single-phase grou nd fault and good tolerance to transition resistance.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Tripping-and-Reclosing Strategy for Grounding Faults on Double-Circuit Wind Power Outgoing Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: When aground fault occurs on double-circuit wind power outgoing lines, the conventional tripping strategy may inject negative sequence components into the system, as well as the traditional automatic reclosing scheme does not determine the fault feature before the reclosing, if it is reclosed to a permanent fault, stability of the power system will be affected. To solve the above problems, an intelligent tripping-and-reclosing strategy for grounding faults on double-circuit wind power outgoing lines is proposed, single-ended phase segregated switches are used in the strategy. Firstly, by establishing and analyzing the phase-to-phase coupling model of double-circuit wind power outgoing lines, a new tripping strategy that can avoid the injection of negative sequence components into the power system is proposed. Secondly, the capacitive coupling voltage characteristics are analyzed under transient and permanent faults, and the fault feature identification criteria based on the capacitive coupling voltage of double-circuit wind power outgoing lines is proposed. Finally, the new tripping and closing strategy are combined to form an intelligent tripping-and-reclosing strategy for grounding faults on double-circuit wind power outgoing lines. The PSCAD/EMTDC simulation verifies that the proposed strategy can avoid the injection of negative sequence components into the system and ensure the reclosing success rate and stability of wind power transmission lines under different ground fault types, fault locations and transition resistances.

articleTitle: An Auxiliary Directional Relay of Distribution Network with Photovoltaic Source Based on Harmonic Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The integration of distributed photovoltaic power sources into the distribution network leads to the transformation of the original single-source network into a multi-source network, and the existing overcurrent protection is prone to misoperation under the action of reverse photovoltaic currents. An auxiliary fault directional relay based on harmonic energy is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the fault current output of PV and system power sources are derived separately, and the difference of harmonic output between the two sources during the fault is pointed out. Then, after avoiding part of the attenuated DC time, the sub-mode is extracted using the variational modal decomposition(VMD) method to characterize the current harmonic signal in the required frequency band. Secondly, the signal energy ratio within the protection time window is calculated to reduce the interference of noise and other factors, and the fault direction discrimination results are output. Finally, the correctness of the proposed directional element is verified by simulation. The directional relay does not require communication, does not require voltage quantities, and can identify the source direction of the fault current quickly and reliably.

articleTitle: A Non-Pilot Protection Scheme for Transmission Lines Connected to Inverter-Interfaced Power Source
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The fault characteristics of transmission lines connected to inverter-interfaced power sources such as photovoltaic stations and permanent magnetic synchronous generator are fundamentally different from traditional power grids, and traditional protection methods have adaptability issues. The protection on the system side and the inverter side of the transmission line has inconsistent characteristics of sensitivity, reliability, and speed. When the system side protection operates and controls breaker tripping, the distance protection on the station side then can operate reliably in a longer time. In this regard, this article proposes a non-pilot protection scheme that utilizes low sampling rate single ended electrical quantities. For different types of faults, zero sequence current, negative sequence current, and voltage harmonic components are used as acceleration criteria for distance protection, which can reliably accelerate the local distance protection action after the opposite breaker trips. A photovoltaic station transmission system model is built in PSCAD, and the simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Smart Tripping and Closing Strategy for Line-to-Line Un-Grounding Faults of the Wind Farm Double-Circuit Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The quasi-three-phase tripping strategy of the double-circuit transmission line can improve the reliability of power supply compared with the traditional automatic reclosing strategy, but some complex types of faults will still interrupt the power supply by tripping the whole phase, as well as reclosing without distinguishing the nature of the fault by rectifying the time, a secondary impact will be caused to the system if reclosing in permanent faults. To address the above problems, a smart tripping and closing strategy for line-to-line un-grounding faults of the wind farm double-circuit transmission line based on the fault phase voltage characteristics is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the inter-phase coupling characteristics of faults in quasi-three-phase operation mode is analyzed, and a new tripping strategy based on quasi-three-phase operation mode is proposed, ensuring continuous power supply while building inter-phase coupling circuit; secondly, to establish the equivalent circuit of permanent and transient faults, the fault nature criteria is proposed based on the two fault phase voltage difference characteristics. Then a smart tripping and closing strategy for the wind farm double-circuit transmission line line-to-line un-grounding faults is proposed. Finally, the simulation results show the correctness of the strategy.

Author Keywords: double-circuit transmission line on the same tower

articleTitle: Construction and Applications of Knowledge Graph of Relay Protection Device Defects Based On Ne04J and Structured Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The defect data of relay protection device contains rich operation and maintenance management information that needs to be excavated, and its effective utilization is of great significance for improving the reliability of relay protection system operation. This paper constructs a knowledge graph based on Neo4j for the structured data of relay protection device defect records, and implements the related applications, and completes the information mining work. Specifically, firstly, the powerful data retrieval and screening function based on Neo4j knowledge graph is explained from the basic theory; secondly, the structured data is divided into corresponding nodes and attribute relations according to the construction logic graph, and the Neo4j-based knowledge graph is formed; finally, the nodes and attributes matching method is adopted to traverse and retrieve the structured data knowledge graph, and the online query of defect type and statistical analysis of equipment performance of each manufacturer are realized.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Differential Protection Based on Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Current differential protection is a widely adopted and effective high-voltage AC transmission line protection scheme. The long distance of the transmission line determines that the distributed parameters and corresponding capacitive currents are not negligible. In fact, the physical laws of a distributed parameter transmission line can be expressed as a set of partial differential equations (PDEs). In this paper, a time-domain current differential protection method based on two-terminal electrical quantities and the PDE line model is proposed. The method does not depend on the power frequency phasors, can accurately compensate line capacitive current, and can effectively improve the protection speed and sensitivity. Numerical experiments validate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method. Additionally, the proposed method demonstrates satisfactory real-time performance under relatively low sampling rates (4k Hz).

articleTitle: MMC Circulation Suppression Optimization Strategy Based on Quasi-$\text{PI}^{\lambda}\mathrm{R}$ Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: To suppress the circulating current in modular multilevel converters (MMC), this paper analyzes MMC's operating characteristics and mechanism. Based on the poor suppression effect and slow adjustment time of traditional quasi-PR circulating current suppressors, a suppression method based on quasi-PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>R suppressors is studied. By introducing a fractional order integration link based on quasi-PR circulating current suppressors, the Whale Optimization Algorithm(WOA) was used to optimize the fractional order parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> to obtain the optimal value, while analyzing the stability of the system. Under the action of a quasi-PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>R suppressor, the second harmonic component was better suppressed and the adjustment time was shortened. And compare and analyze the system performance using traditional PR suppressors and quasi-PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>R suppressors respectively. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed suppression method was verified through simulation.

articleTitle: A Pilot Protection for Transmission Lines Connected to Wind Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Due to the influence of the complex control, the short circuit current provided by wind power generation units exhibits new characteristics, such as controlled amplitude and phase and weak feedback characteristics, affecting the performance of traditional protections. This paper proposes a novel pilot protection using the compensated voltage on both sides. The proposed method has a strong anti-fault resistance ability and has no need for data synchronization. The test results indicate that the proposed method can distinguish the internal faults and external fault reliably, unaffected by the new characteristics of short circuit current.

articleTitle: Automatic Graph Modeling of Power Transformer Management Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Data for electrical components is maintained by different information systems in China. Currently, the relational database is commonly used to obtain and manage data for equipment maintenance purposes. However, as the modern power system develops, there is a growing need for massive data processing from different sources, which poses challenges to relational databases of its limitations in model flexibility, query efficiency, and scalability. Compared to traditional relational databases, graph databases handle fast-changing, inter-connected data well, offer flexibility, and have higher query efficiency. This paper introduces a graph modeling technique for transformer equipment to quickly acquire and maintain data for transformer equipment operation and management purposes. An initial data screening is performed to select data with different sources, structures, and characteristics. Word2vec and K-means are adapted to define and cluster model candidate sets. TextRank is applied to perform disambiguation for those transformer model sets. The transformer management graph model is then optimized based on its business scenario. The automatic resulting model provides comprehensive transformer data management, which opens transformer equipment operation and maintenance scenarios. This work significantly improves transformer automatic modeling and data management efficiency and compatibility. The results demonstrate the importance and potential of applying graph database in electrical component data management.

articleTitle: Accurate Detection Method for Voltage Traveling Wave Based on L1-Regularization and Least Squares Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the secondary traveling wave obtained by the voltage traveling wave sensor cannot truly reflect the waveform and fault information of the primary traveling wave, this paper proposes an accurate detection method for voltage traveling wave based on L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-regularization and least squares optimization. Firstly, the forward transfer function model of the special voltage traveling wave sensor is constructed, and then the inversion model is derived. Then, discrete deconvolution method and L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-regularization and least squares inversion algorithm are used to obtain the primary traveling wave signal. Simulation and experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively solve the ill-posed problem in waveform inversion. The similarity between the inversion and simulation of the primary traveling wave is high, and the accurate detection of fault transient traveling wave information can be realized.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Insights into Resistive Superconducting Fault Current Limiter Integration for Enhanced Stability in a German Power Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical investigation of a resistive superconducting fault current limiter (R-SFCL) integrated into a real German power grid. The power system under consideration exhibits a high level of fault current and a rapid rate of transient recovery voltage. Therefore, we propose a comprehensive modeling approach for the R-SFCL based on second-generation high-temperature superconductor tapes, utilizing MATLAB Simulink.Our simulation results demonstrate that the R-SFCL not only effectively limits fault currents to desired levels but also significantly enhances the transient recovery voltage of circuit breakers. This research contributes valuable insights into the application of R-SFCL technology to improve the overall stability and performance of power distribution systems.

articleTitle: A Frequency Support Strategy of Multiple Wind Power Plants Based on Consensus Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In recent years, as renewable energy-based generation are increasing, the concern about the frequency stability and inertia has raised in power systems. To address these issues, various virtual inertia control methods for wind turbine (WT) by utilizing the rotor's kinetic energy (KE) have been recently developed. Moreover, as the penetration level of wind farms (WFs) continues to increase, conventional centralized control schemes face challenges such as time delays or communication failures. In addition, existing distributed control for WFs does not adequately consider the individual operating states of each WT. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a consensus-based distributed control scheme that considers the amount of KE stored in each WT, ensuring an effective frequency response (FR). In addition, a rotor speed recovery control strategy is developed to prevent secondary frequency drop (SFD) caused by sudden reductions of WT's output. The proposed distributed control scheme can provide temporary FR without excessive deceleration of rotor speed and reduce the SFD simultaneously. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control approach is validated through a case study based on PSCAD/EMTDC simulation.

articleTitle: The Definition of Effective Inertia and its Analysis on the Low Inertia System Connected via HVDC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of “Effective Inertia,” which refers to the kinetic energy contributed by synchronous generators up to a specific frequency threshold. Additionally, the notion of “Critical Effective Inertia” is proposed, representing the energy required until the lowest point of frequency. By quantifying these energy values, it becomes possible to determine the additional energy needed to maintain frequency stability. However, when evaluating effective inertia, it is crucial to account for Fast Frequency Response (FFR) mechanisms, such as HVDC, as they possess distinct dynamic characteristics. To demonstrate the application of this concept, a case study of the Jeju power system in South Korea is presented, focusing on the analysis of effective inertia in a low inertia system connected via HVDC.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Sensor Arrays in Electromagnetic Tomography for Non-Destructive Treeing Detection in XLPE Cables
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: XLPE cables are prone to insulation aging faults such as water trees and electrical trees during long-term operation. Once treeing defects occur, they could lead to discharge or breakdown in XLPE cable, seriously threaten the safe and stable operation of the power grid. Accurate positioning and detection of treeing defects has become an urgent need for cable condition monitoring. Electromagnetic tomography (EMT) has the advantages of non-invasive, non-contact, and permeable through metal media, and is expected to be applied in non-destructive testing of treeing faults in XLPE cables. The precision of EMT system highly relies on the hardware design of sensor arrays. To explore the exact relationship between structural design of sensor arrays and the quality of electromagnetic tomography imaging, this paper optimizes the sensor array by changing the number of coils in the sensor array and modifying the traditional coil structure to a coaxial differential structure. The sensor array with different structures is modelled in COMSOL Multiphysics finite element software, and Tikhonov algorithm is used to solve the inverse problem of internal space reconstructions in XPLE cables by EMT imaging. Treeing defects with different sizes and locations are modelled and the imaging effects are compared. Research results indicate that by increasing the number of sensors, imaging quality can be improved accordingly. The usage of coaxial differential structure can eliminate the influence of excitation magnetic field and improve the accuracy of image reconstruction for treeing defects. Research work in this paper has can be a good reference for the setting of sensor arrays in the next step of EMT system design.

articleTitle: Copula Theory Based Calculation Method of Fault Probability Under Typhoons Disaster
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Extreme natural disasters like typhoons, occurs infrequently but cause serious damage. However, typhoons are often accompanied by heavy rainfall, which may also cause line breaks and fallen towers. In this paper, a method for calculating the fault probability under typhoons and rainstorms using Copula theory and Generalized Pareto Distribution (GPD) is proposed. First, based on GPDs of wind speed and rainfall under typhoon weather, the calculation models of wind and rain loads are proposed. Furthermore, considering the relevance between wind and rain loads imposed on towers and power lines, a joint probability distribution calculation model for wind and rain loads is proposed using Copula theory. On this basis, the probability calculation of line breaks and towers fallen under typhoon disaster is realized. Finally, the proposed method is validated by comparing with the fault probability calculation methods without considering coupling of wind speed and rainfall.

Author Keywords: power line breaks and fallen towers

articleTitle: Differential Protection for Double-Ended Weak-Infeed Transmission Lines Based on Time-Domain Integral Value of Traveling Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: For MMC-HVDC systems connected with PV power plants, the converters on both sides of the AC transmission line will adopt different fault-ride-through strategies, making the fault characteristics of the line complicated. Under complex fault characteristics, traditional protection schemes such as current differential protection face challenges such as the reduced sensitivity. In this paper, a differential protection scheme is proposed based on fault traveling wave theory, and an auxiliary criterion using wavelet transform is proposed to ensure accurate identification of fault interval while achieving high sensitivity. The proposed scheme has been verified in PSCAD/EMTDC, and simulation results show that the proposed method is a highly sensible protection scheme suitable for double-ended weak-infeed lines between large-scale renewable energy and MMC stations.

articleTitle: Modeling of Tree Contact Faults in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Tree contact is a common and potentially hazardous fault in distribution networks. Due to the high resistance and low grounding current associated with tree contact faults, traditional protective devices often fail to detect and trigger at the appropriate threshold levels. However, the presence of undetected tree contact faults for extended periods can lead to dangerous situations, such as the outbreak of wildfires. Existing high-resistance fault models are inadequate in reflecting the mechanisms of tree contact and accurately identifying such faults. This research addresses these limitations by analyzing the physical mechanisms underlying tree contact and developing an improved modeling approach for identifying these faults. The modeling approach considers various factors such as arc characteristics, the influence of temperature on conductivity, and the impact of tree trunk moisture on conductivity. By incorporating these factors into the fault model, a more comprehensive representation of the fault mechanism is achieved. The process of tree contact is divided into multiple stages, and equivalent models are constructed based on the actual physical processes involved. Through comparative analysis with real waveform data, it is demonstrated that the proposed fault models effectively capture the evolutionary process of tree contact faults. The results of this study contribute to the understanding of tree contact faults and their impact on distribution networks. The developed modeling approach, considering arc characteristics, temperature effects, and tree trunk moisture content, provides a more comprehensive and accurate representation of the fault mechanism, facilitating improved fault detection and prevention.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis of Power System Considering Traction Load
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The influence of traction load access on the transient stability of power system is discussed. Firstly, based on the analysis of the operating characteristics of traction load, an improved traction load model is proposed, and the equivalent parameters of the improved traction load model are solved according to the genetic algorithm. Secondly, based on the Power System Analysis Software Package (PSASP), a power system simulation model with traction load is established, and a traction load model is connected to the power system for transient stability analysis and calculation. Finally, based on the power system simulation model with traction load, the influence of different speed traction load and different proportion of traction load on power system transient stability calculation is analyzed, and the influence of traction load and common load on power system transient stability calculation is compared and analyzed. The results show that the access of traction load has a certain impact on the transient stability margin of the power system. The higher the locomotive speed in the traction load, the more serious the impact on the transient stability of the power system. The higher the proportion of traction load in the power system, the smaller the limit clearing time when the near fault occurs in the power system.

articleTitle: An Accurate Under Frequency Load Shedding Method for the Active Distribution Grid with Distributed Generators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Under frequency load shedding(UFLS) is essential to maintain the frequency stability of low inertia power systems that are subjected to a disturbance of power deficit. However, the increasing integration of renewable energy sources(RESs) and distributed generators(DGs) in the distribution grid significantly changes the dynamics of power systems, posing new challenges as well as opportunities for UFLS. To this end, an accurate UFLS method is proposed for the distribution grid in this paper. Firstly, the optimization model of UFLS is proposed, in which the idea of active islanding is first introduced into UFLS control. Then the frequency dynamics of load and DGs are taken into consideration, thus the frequency error constraints are constructed for this optimization problem. Finally, the method is tested in the modified IEEE 69-bus power distribution system. Simulation results verify the proposed method's accuracy, efficiency, and effectiveness.

articleTitle: High-Precision Wide-Range Current Transformer Based on Compensation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Current transformers (CTs) are critical devices in power systems, and their measurement accuracy directly affects the safety and stability of the power grid. This paper proposes a compensation algorithm for CTs to enhance measurement precision effectively. Firstly, offline measurements of the primary and secondary side currents and the magnetic flux of the CT under different operational conditions are conducted. A model of the magnetic flux versus excitation current curve is fitted from this. With the help of this fitted model, during online measurements, the excitation current is obtained from the magnetic flux, which is then used to compensate for the secondary current. To verify the performance of the proposed method, this paper conducted validations through simulations and physical experiments. In EMTP-RV, simulations were conducted based on the data from actual 10P10-rated protection CTs, choosing several known and unknown operating conditions. A physical experimental platform was set up for compensation experiments on closed and open-type 10P10 protection CTs. Both simulation and physical experimental results indicate that the proposed method can effectively enhance the measurement accuracy of wide-range CTs, validating the feasibility of high-precision wide-range CTs.

articleTitle: Traveling Wave Protection for the AC Transmission Lines between MMC Stations and Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Several MMC-HVDC systems with renewable energy sources connected have been constructed in the past decades. For the AC transmission lines between the MMC stations and the renewable energy sources, fault-ride-through strategies at both ends will lead to complicated fault characteristics. Specifically, the current amplitudes are restricted and the phase angles are controlled, the characteristics decrease the reliability and sensitivity of traditional relay protection. This paper proposes a differential protection based on the traveling wave theory, which focuses on the transmission lines and excludes the influence of the power sources outside the protected area. Criterion is constructed based on the integral value of the amplitude of the traveling wave differential current. The proposed protection is verified in a PSCAD simulation model. Test results prove that, compared with traditional current differential protection, the traveling wave differential protection has advantages in reliability, and the ability to withstand fault resistance.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of the New Energy Development in Major International Economies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Developing new energy has a positive impact on promoting environmental sustainability and improving the living environment for human beings. Promoting the comprehensive upgrading of energy structure and vigorously developing new energy is an important way for China to achieve the “dual carbon” goal. This article analyzes the development of new energy in major international economies such as Germany, France, Spain, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Japan based on three dimensions of new energy development indicators, policies in the field of new energy, and consumption measures. Based on their development characteristics, it provides new ideas for China's new energy development, thereby improving China's level of new energy consumption and promoting the healthy development of new energy in China.

articleTitle: A Dynamic State Estimation Method Based on Robust Cubature Kalman Filter and Super Phasor Measurement Units
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for dynamic state estimation (DSE) in power systems, leveraging the integration of robust cubature Kalman filter (RCKF) and Super Phasor Measurement Unit (SPMU) measurements. The proposed RCKF can identify and down-weight the bad data based on normalized innovations. The SPMU measurements with superior refresh rate and expanded measurement capabilities compared to regular PMUs can enhance both the accuracy and robustness of the DSE. Simulations results carried out in IEEE 14-bus test system demonstrate the the superior performance of our proposed method in terms of both accuracy and robustness against bad data.

articleTitle: Analysis of Transient Process of Photovoltaic System in a New Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the proposal of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals and the construction of new power systems, the proportion of new energy generation in the power system continues to increase. As a major component of new energy generation, analyzing and understanding the transient process and characteristics of photovoltaic power generation systems can provide a theoretical basis for transient based protection. The switching of power electronic equipment operation strategies during normal operation and failure of photovoltaic power generation systems will trigger transient processes in the system. This article studies photovoltaic power generation systems, aiming to analyze the transient process of photovoltaic access systems and its analytical expression. At present, the transient process analysis of output fluctuations in photovoltaic power generation systems mainly relies on simulation analysis, which is limited by specific scenarios and lacks interpretability. This article first establishes the characteristics and characterization methods of photovoltaic wave motion through actual data. Next, consider the control strategies at the photovoltaic boost circuit and inverter circuit, and analyze the impact of these two control strategies on output fluctuations and fault transients. Finally, a transfer function expression is established from the control block diagram, and based on the input changes of the reference value of the control system during sudden changes in photovoltaic output, two transient analytical expressions of the photovoltaic power generation system are obtained. The specific transient expression analytical expressions during output fluctuations provide theoretical support for future research based on transient protection.

articleTitle: Upward Streamer Behaviour on ESE Lightning Rod Employing Field Electron Emission Model Under Lightning Impulse Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the upward streamer behavior on early streamer emission (ESE) lightning rod. In the case of ESE lightning rod, it is based on the concept of Inductance and conductance (L-C) resonant circuit to occur early corona discharge propagation. In other words, the upward streamer can be controlled by adjusting electron emission according to resonance conditions. In this paper, to analyze the possibility of upward streamer control according to electron emission under high electric field, Fowler-Nordheim equation was employed for the boundary condition on the surface of ESE lightning rod. To control the emitted electron from the surface of ESE lightning rod, the work function (ϕ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf>) of the aluminum material was controlled from 3.8 to 4.0 eV. The results revealed that the emitted electron density increases with decreasing work function of aluminum, it might be possible that the control of electron emission by resonance conditions could be having a larger protection radius Δ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> than that of a conventional franklin lightning rod.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Different Grounding Methods on the DC Side During Steady-State Operation of Low-Voltage DC Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: This research presents a comparative analysis of the effects of various grounding methods at the DC side of the Low-Voltage DC (LV-DC) distribution network, employing a single two-level voltage source converter (VSC). The study investigates how different DC-side grounding configurations influence the steady-state operation of the distribution system. An assessment framework is established using three critical steady-state performance indicators: common-mode voltage, zero-sequence current to ground, and leakage current. The analysis begins with the derivation of the common-mode voltage expression based on the VSC structure. Subsequently, employing bilateral Fourier decomposition of the AC voltage at the VSC valve side, the zero-sequence equivalent circuit for the three-phase VSC is deduced, along with the calculation expression for zero-sequence current to ground. The research further delves into the generation of leakage current and its influencing factors, following established definitions. Lastly, by comprehensively analyzing the influencing factors of the three steady-state indicators and contrasting the effects of different DC-side grounding methods on system stability, the study concludes that a non-grounded DC side exhibits superior steady-state operational characteristics, a conclusion substantiated through simulation verification.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of SCR on Different Modes Dominated by Heterogeneous Synchronous Control of Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the large-scale increase in phase-locked loop (PLL) synchronous grid-connected converters in the power system, the system grid strength or short-circuit ratio (SCR) is relatively reduced, resulting in frequent oscillation problems dominated by PLL in the system. The external characteristics of grid-forming converters contribute to the grid strength but are limited by the black-box nature of the converter dynamic model. In addition, SCR is generally used as an evaluation index of grid strength in engineering applications. However, existing research has not yet fully revealed the mechanism of grid strength in heterogeneous converter grid-connected systems. Therefore, this paper first establishes the frequency domain admittance and impedance models corresponding to the grid-following converter and the grid-forming converter respectively, based on the duality of the PLL control and virtual synchronous control. Then, by analyzing the small disturbance stability of a single-converter grid-connected system, the influence of SCR on different dominant modes of heterogeneous synchronous control converter is clarified. Finally, the analysis results were simulated and verified in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: A Study on Transmission Line Protection Using Incident Current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Modern traveling wave-based (TW-based) protection solutions for transmission lines have been increasingly adopted in real-world power systems. Among various methods, the Differentiator Smoother (DS) filter is a mature signal processing technique, relying on high-frequency sampled data, and has been used in commercially available TW-based relays. The DS filtering technique extracts the transients, related to fault-induced TWs in the measured currents, which are a superposition of the incident and reflected waves. The magnitude of this transient, which is dependent on the termination characteristics of the transmission line, could be very small, if the termination impedance is significantly higher than the characteristic impedance of the transmission line, potentially resulting in poor accuracy in fault location estimation. In this paper, a study on Transmission Line Protection based on the incident current is presented. Real-time simulations are performed using RTDS® real-time digital simulator to compare the incident current-based method with the existing DS-based solution. The results prove a great potential to incorporate such an incident-current based TW protection solution into commercially available TW-based relays.

articleTitle: Research on Shore DC Grids Considering Increasing Penetration of Renewables
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the increasing severity of global climate change, the implementation of green ports and the utilization of renewables have become imperative for sustainable shore development. However, with the increasing penetration of renewables, numerous power electronic converters in conventional shore AC grids (SACGs) results in higher investment and operation costs, while also diminishing the overall system's efficiency and reliability. This paper begins by introducing the shore DC grid (SDCG) considering the growing penetration of renewables and the battery-powered ships. Next, the advantages and the practical issues associated with SDCGs are summarized. Finally, three feasible topological structures of SDCGs are discussed. This research can serve as a reference for the implementation and development of SDCGs.

articleTitle: Data Compression for Differential Protection of Distribution Network: A Wavelet Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the ever-increasing integration of high proportions of renewable energy sources, the distribution network is gradually becoming a multi-source grid. Differential protection could remove the fault line from both sides and has good protective performance in transmission network. However, differential protection has a high requirement for time delay and communication capacity, making it difficult to be applied to distribution networks. This paper analyzes the data compression requirements of differential protection in distribution network and presents a data compression scheme based on the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) for differential protection. To verify the effectiveness, a 10kV distribution network simulation model was established in PSCAD/EMTDC. The data demonstrates the feasibility of the DWT-based data compression algorithm for differential protection. Finally, this paper discusses the selection of wavelet decomposition level and wavelet function and their influence on data compression performance.

articleTitle: A Coordinated Optimization Control Strategy for Transient Stability of the Multi-infeed HVDC Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In response to deal with transient frequency and voltage stability caused by large-capacity DC blocking fault in multi-infeed HVDC receiving-end power grid, a coordinated optimization control strategy considering HVDC power increase, AC filter switching, synchronous condenser excitation control and load shedding is proposed. The control sensitivity of transient stability margin is calculated by using the trajectory sensitivity method based on the time domain simulation results of PSD-BP A software. According to the interlocking relationship between DC active power and AC filter reactive power, the single function expression of the constrain is derived. Aiming at minimizing the control cost, an optimization model for coordinated control of multiple control methods is established, which takes the transient stability margin as the constrains and considers the control cost difference and weight priority of each variable. Based on C++ platform, the parallel simulation calculation and optimization model solution are implemented. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified by the case study of East China Power Grid

articleTitle: High Sensitivity Differential Protection for AC Line in MMC-HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Due to the influence of MMC control mode, the differential protection of AC transmission line in MMC-HVDC system has low sensitivity. To solve this problem, a high sensitivity differential protection scheme based on phase correction is proposed. The phase offset affected by the control link is calculated and the additional phase Angle is obtained. The additional phase Angle is introduced in the calculation of differential protection. In view of different fault phases, positive and negative sequence current is used to correct the phase. The influence of MMC control strategy on differential protection is reduced. The scheme can effectively identify faults and has high sensitivity. At the same time, it can adapt to different operation modes of MMC and has strong resistance to transition resistance.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Transient Simulation Modelling and Analysis of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: High-power chargers using modern power electronics are highly non-linear power consumption devices that generate harmonic pollution to the power grid. In contrast, a high-current power supply takes less time and is favourable to the promotion of electric vehicles, but the harmonic currents generated during charging will degrade the power quality of the power system. In this paper, a simplified model of the charger is proposed, in which a nonlinear resistor R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> is used to approximately simulate the equivalent input resistance of the high-frequency power conversion link, and the correspondence between the charging power and the equivalent resistance is given. Based on the data of a demonstration charging station, a single-machine grid-connected model as well as a multi-machine grid-connected model are constructed on the ADPSS platform, and harmonic analyses of the charging station are carried out, focusing on the study of the harmonic current containment rate of each harmonic, and the law of the total harmonic distortion rate of the current with the change of charging power of the electric vehicle.

articleTitle: VSC-HVDC Line Reclosing Strategy Based on Parallel Branch Trial
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Conventional flexible DC transmission lines can be blindly reclosed without distinguishing the nature of the fault, and if they are reclosed in the case of a permanent fault, the resulting secondary overcurrent shock can cause serious damage to costly and fragile DC equipment. Therefore, an adaptive reclosing strategy for flexible DC transmission lines with additional test branch is proposed. The scheme adds a test branch to the large DC capacitor that can be re-integrated into the system after a trip and injects electrical quantities into the line through the capacitor in the test branch as a criterion. The voltage in case of transient fault remains basically constant, while the voltage in case of permanent fault drops rapidly to 0. Therefore, this paper identifies the nature of the fault with the help of the integration of the test branch voltage. Finally, a simulation model is built using PSCAD/EMTDC software, and the simulation verifies that the proposed scheme is not affected by the transition resistance and can effectively distinguish between permanent and transient faults.

articleTitle: The Impact of Cross Line Different-Phase Successive Faults on Fault Detection Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: At present, the technology of single phase ground fault line selection in small current earthing system is relatively mature, but when a single phase ground fault occurs in the system, the non fault phase voltage increases, which is likely to lead to breakdown of the non fault phase insulation weak point, forming a second ground fault, which turns into a cross line different-phase successive fault. For the detection of cross line different-phase successive fault, there are still some problems with the current line selection device. Often, only the first ground fault can be detected, while the second ground fault is not handled. When a cross line different-phase successive fault occurs on site, the line selection device often only selects the first ground fault line, and the staff judges another fault line, which results in a long fault duration and long power recovery time. It is not conducive to the safe and stable operation of the distribution network, so further research is needed for the detection of cross line different-phase successive fault. This article combines real fault cases and simulation data on site to analyze the causes and development process of cross line different phase successive fault. It also analyzes the changes in various electrical quantities during the process of transitioning from single-phase grounding faults to cross line different phase successive fault, and analyzes the impact of cross line different-phase successive fault on existing small current grounding line selection devices, Finally, improvement suggestions were proposed to address the occurrence of cross line different-phase successive fault.

articleTitle: Investigation of Fracture Mechanism and Performance Optimization of Grading Electrode Applied in HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Grading electrode is widely used to the converter valve in the high voltage direct current (HVDC) system for balancing the voltage between the components and protecting components from electrolytic corrosion. The grading electrode is made of pure Pt in a needle shape. Recently, some Pt electrode needles fractured during service which should be paid more attention. Multiple fracture causes have been analyzed utilizing a combination methods of chemical composition analysis, mechanical property test, fracture surface observation and microstructure observation.
