It is demonstrated that the failure mechanism of the Pt needle is fatigue fracture. This mainly due to the low shear strength of the Pt needle, which is around 140MPa. In order to increase the safety and reliability of grading electrode during service, the processing technology of the Pt needles has been optimized. The microstructure of the Pt needle has been improved and the shear strength has been increased to 297MPa.

articleTitle: Analytical Assessment of Reactive Power Support Capacity for DFIGs Under Voltage Drop Failure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Since the reactive power support capacity of the doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) during grid failures can be scheduled within a certain range, DFIGs are used as an effective and controllable reactive power source to support the AC grid voltage. However, the nonlinearity of the power flow equations in wind farms and the uncertainty of the reactive power range of DFIGs limit the accurate assessment of the reactive power support capacity of DFIG-based wind farms. To this end, this paper proposes a reactive power support capability evaluation method considering the internal and external constraints of DFIG operations. By focusing on the impacts of the rotor current and the coupling between the terminal voltage and reactive power on the allowable reactive power support capacity of DFIGs, analytical constraints of allowable reactive power of DFIGs under voltage drop are analyzed. At last, with the time domain simulation analysis, the allowable reactive power range of DFIGs considering internal and external constraints is verified.

articleTitle: State Evaluation of Secondary Equipment Based on Matter-Element Extension Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of single evaluation index, strong subjectivity and lack of accuracy of evaluation results in the traditional evaluation model of secondary equipment in power system, a comprehensive evaluation method of secondary equipment operation status based on matter-element extension theory is proposed. First, build a comprehensive evaluation index system for the operation status of secondary equipment. Secondly, the subjective and objective weights of the evaluation indicators are calculated based on the attribute hierarchy model and the anti-entropy weight method. On this basis, the combined weights are calculated using the cooperative game model. Finally, based on matter-element extension theory, a comprehensive evaluation model of secondary equipment operation status is built. The case analysis shows that this method can improve the rationality and accuracy of the secondary equipment condition evaluation results, and provide effective assistance for the operation, maintenance and repair of secondary equipment.

articleTitle: A Novel Principle of Current Differential Protection for Renewable Energy Station
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In the context of building a new power system dominated by renewable energy sources, the integration of high proportion of renewable energy and high proportion of power electronic equipment imposes stricter requirements on power system protection. The current differential protection, as the main protection for the outgoing line of renewable energy stations, has a significant impact on the development and utilization of renewable energy and the stable operation of the power grid. Most of the existing studies start from the specific fault characteristics of renewable energy sources, and improve the performance of differential protection by modifying and supplementing criteria. This paper analyzes the phase and amplitude relationships of each phase current on both sides of the outgoing line of the renewable energy station, proposes a novel principle of current differential protection based on cross compensation, and verify the performance of proposed protection by building a model in PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Transient Characteristics Analysis of High Impedance Ground Fault in High-Speed Railway Traction Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: When a high impedance ground fault occurs in the high-speed railway traction network, the fault electrical quantities are relatively weak, and the traditional fault identification method using steady-state fault information is not effective. Therefore, this paper builds a high-speed railway traction network high impedance ground fault transient model in the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation platform based on the arc characteristics under the transient of high-impedance faults. By simulating and analyzing the transient changes of traveling wave currents under different fault conditions, the impact of multiple factors such as fault location, transition resistance, initial phase angle, and train position on high impedance ground faults in the traction network is summarized, and the propagation characteristics of transient current traveling waves for high impedance ground faults are outlined. This provides a research idea for identifying high-frequency traveling wave signals under high impedance faults in subsequent transient conditions of high-speed railway traction networks.

articleTitle: A Grounding Fault Protection Method for Low Resistance Grounded Distribution Networks Based on Capacity Current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: When a single-phase grounding fault occurs in a low resistance grounded distribution network, the threshold for zero-sequence overcurrent protection is often set based on the principle of avoiding the maximum capacity current of the non-fault line. Due to the high threshold value, the protection will refuse to operate under high resistance grounding conditions. This paper proposes a grounding fault protection method for low resistance grounded distribution networks based on capacity current compensation on the basis of the existing zero-sequence overcurrent protection. This method serves as a backup protection for the existing overcurrent protection. When the low resistance grounding fault occurs, the existing protection operates. When the high resistance grounding fault occurs, the existing protection refuses to operate. The zero-sequence current of each outgoing line is compensated using the bus voltage and line capacity parameters, and the ratio after and before compensation is calculated. By comparing this ratio with the protection threshold in this paper, reliable operation of the protection in case of high resistance grounding faults can be achieved. After theoretical derivation and model simulation, this method can cope with stable grounding faults and the ability to handle fault resistance can reach about 4000.

articleTitle: Allocation and Optimal Operation Strategy of Distributed Energy Storage with High Ratio PV
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The configuration and optimal operation of Distributed Energy Storage (DES) can reduce the adverse effects of high proportional PV access on grid operation. In this paper, we consider the voltage characteristics of the low-voltage station area with high proportion of PV access, and divide the mandatory charging time and non-mandatory charging time for DES configuration and optimal operation according to the voltage amplitude, and solve the DES location and capacity problem with the lowest cost of DES configuration as the optimization objective during the mandatory charging time, and the optimal operation of DES with the minimization of station loss as the optimization objective during the non-mandatory charging time. The objective function is solved using the particle swarm algorithm. The results of the analysis of the IEEE-33 nodes system show that the DES configuration and optimal operation strategy proposed in this paper is feasible.

articleTitle: Research on Reclosing and Fault Location Methods for 1000kV UHV Overhead-GIL Hybrid Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The requirements for reclosing are different for ultra-high voltage overhead-GIL hybrid transmission lines during faults in overhead and GIL sections, and the parameters of each section of the line are uneven, making it difficult to accurately locate faults. Therefore, line reclosing and fault location face special problems. A protection system with fault section positioning function suitable for overhead-GIL hybrid lines is proposed in the article. This system adds a set of differential protection in the GIL section, forming a configuration scheme of “ Large Range Differential Protection (LRDP)“ and” Small Range Differential Protection (SRDP)” for line protection. Using LRDP and SRDP to determine whether the fault occurred in the overhead line section or the GIL section, the adaptive reclosing of the fault section is realized. Using LRDP and SRDP action results and SRDP direction discrimination results, the fault section is determined, and then the fault can be accurately located using a dual terminal fault location method based on distributed parameter model. Simulation tests show that the proposed method can accurately locate fault sections in hybrid lines, achieve adaptive reclosing of fault sections, and accurately locate fault in hybrid lines.

articleTitle: High Impedance Fault Detection Method Based on Traveling Wave Full Waveform Fault Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: High impedance ground fault (HIF) occurs in a distribution network, the fault features are weak and susceptible to factors such as noise interference. Extracting and detecting the wavefronts in this case can be challenging, leading to low reliability in HIF detection methods based on waveforms. To address these issues, this paper proposes an HIF detection method based on self-recognition of fault features using traveling wave full waveform (TWFW) characteristics. Firstly, it analyzes the differences between HIF and normal transient disturbances wave signals in the time-frequency domain based on TWFW. Then, it utilizes a CBAM-CNN neural network model to explore fault features from TWFW grayscale images from multiple dimensions, enhancing the method's fault detection and interference resistance capabilities. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a high detection accuracy of up to 99.8%, reliably detects HIF, exhibits excellent noise resistance, and is unaffected by factors such as fault location and fault impedance.

articleTitle: A Study on the System Strength Evaluation Index Considering the Interaction Between Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In order to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the connection of renewable energy to power system is increasing. Renewable energy such as wind power and photovoltaic are inverter-based resources (IBRs) that provide limited short-circuit current unlike synchronous generators, and the limited short-circuit current adversely affects voltage after disturbance. Describes Short Circuit Ratio(SCR), a system strength evaluation index used in power systems when connecting inverter-based resources, and Weighted Short Circuit Ratio(WSCR) and Composite Short Circuit Ratio(CSCR), system strength evaluation indexes considering the interaction between inverter-based resources caused by Phased-Locked Loop(PLL) control characteristics is analyzed.

articleTitle: Design of Distributed Detection System for High Voltage Intelligent Breaker Secondary System Based on Dynamic Closed Loop
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The reliable response of the secondary system is a prerequisite for the effective action of intelligent breaker.To solve the problems of cumbersome testing operations, lack of reliability verification methods, and difficulty in identifying hidden defects in the secondary system of high-voltage intelligent breaker, a distributed detection system design method for high-voltage intelligent breaker secondary system based on dynamic closed-loop is proposed. Based on the analysis of the operating principle of the secondary system of high-voltage intelligent breaker, a distributed structure and modular design are adopted. Local wireless communication is used to establish a distributed detection method for the secondary system of high-voltage intelligent breaker under a closed-loop system by unifying clock module labeling. Based on multi-dimensional time series trend analysis and correlation analysis algorithms, a hidden defect identification method for secondary systems was established, and the response time of the intelligent switch secondary circuit was statistically analyzed to identify switch circuit anomalies using confidence intervals. The detection system has been piloted and applied in a 220kV substation, and all detection functions have achieved the expected goals. It provides technical support for the on-site operation and maintenance of high-voltage intelligent breaker and has engineering practical significance.

articleTitle: Fault Section Location of Collector Line in Wind Farm Based on LightGBM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Accurate location of collector line fault section is the key to rapid recovery of collector line fault in wind farms, which is of great significance for solving the problem of electricity transmission stopping and wind power abandonment caused by short circuit fault. Aiming at the problem that the existing wind farm measurement information cannot achieve accurate fault location of collector lines, a fault section location method based on LightGBM algorithm is proposed. Based on the more readily available steady-state current measurement information, the method proposes to add current transformers in each section of the collector line, and takes the variation of the pre-fault and post-fault steady-state RMS values of three-phase currents as the core feature. By building a permanent magnet direct drive wind farm simulation model, the simulation samples under normal operation and fault conditions are obtained. The LightGBM algorithm is used to establish a multi-classification fault segment positioning model offline, which is applied to the wind farm monitoring system to achieve online rapid location of fault sections. MATLAB/SIMULINK experiments verify that the proposed method has good adaptability to collector lines, can accurately locate fault sections in different scenarios, and its positioning performance is less affected by the operation mode, transition resistance and fan power fluctuation.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Control Strategy for Two Terminal Weak Feed Systems Considering Step-Down V/f Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: After an asymmetric fault occurs in a two-terminal weak feed AC system, negative sequence components affect the safe and stable operation of the power system may occur. Therefore, it is necessary to suppress the negative sequence component to improve the stability and reliability of the power system. In this paper, the overcurrent and overvoltage problems caused by negative sequence current · suppression control strategy and negative sequence voltage suppression control strategy on modular multilevel converter (MMC) side are compared. Then, a new control strategy is proposed, which uses the step-down V/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> control strategy and the negative sequence current suppression control strategy on the MMC side to quickly limit the fault current amplitude and effectively avoid the non-fault phase overvoltage. After theoretical analysis and PSCAD simulation, analyze the electrical quantity changes under different types of control strategies. The simulation results show that the proposed fault control strategy effectively limits the negative sequence current amplitude and non-fault phase overvoltage. Under different control strategies, the electrical characteristics of the system vary significantly. The above characteristics can provide a theoretical basis for the analysis of protection adaptability and the study of new protection principles.

articleTitle: Characterization of Frequency Spatial Distribution of Power System Under Disturbance Scenario
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the regional interconnection of UHV AC/DC hybrid grids and the increase in the proportion of renewable energy connected to the grid, the spatial and temporal distribution of frequency response has become increasingly significant. This paper focuses on the spatial distribution characteristics of frequency under the disturbance scenario of power system. The overall study includes the evaluation of spatial distribution characteristics and the unified center of inertia (COI) frequency evaluation. The first step idealizes the network structure by simplifying the DC current matrix. The second step establishes an equivalent model of frequency response of a large power grid with multiple centers of inertia based on the modal analysis method and the superposition of vibration shapes, and performs the frequency oscillation component solution. The third step performs COI frequency calculation by modeling the COI frequency response of a multi-machine system.Finally, simulation is carried out to verify the feasibility of the proposed method, and the influence of disturbance amplitude and location on the spatial distribution characteristics of the frequency response of each node is analyzed.

articleTitle: Calculation of Unbalanced Power Flow in Distribution Networks with Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The existing symmetric component analysis methods cannot provide accurate results and cannot model networks under unbalanced conditions. This article proposes an improved algorithm for calculating the power flow of unbalanced distribution networks containing photovoltaic power based on the forward and backward sweep method. This algorithm has good adaptability to the power flow calculation of distribution networks containing photovoltaic systems. This paper comprehensively analyzes the power flow calculation in three-phase unbalanced distribution networks containing photovoltaic power generation, and points out that the forward and backward sweep method has significant advantages in calculating power flow in distribution networks based on the essential characteristics of each method. A power flow calculation method for unbalanced distribution networks containing new energy sources such as photovoltaic is proposed based on the forward and backward sweep algorithm. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through numerical simulations on a test distribution network that includes distributed generation. Results show the improved accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Application for the Evaluation of Protection Performance in IEC-61850-Based Digital Substations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: A digital substation represents a significant advancement in the field of electrical infrastructure. Unlike conventional substations that rely heavily on analog equipment and manual operations, digital substations embrace automation, data exchange, and real-time monitoring. To secure the interoperability of the communication equipment in the digital substation, IEC 61850 standard is employed for information transformation between devices in the substation. Meanwhile, the data sharing availability in digital substations enhances the protection system to reflect the state of change of the power system, huge amount of data on the local area network (LAN) may cause some problems to the protective intelligent electronic devices (IEDs). The objective of this paper is to develop a digital twin application for evaluating the performance of protection IEDs in IEC 61850 based digital substation. Instead of requiring an expensive real-time digital simulator and actual merging units (MUs), Power System Computer-Aided Design (PSCAD) with digital twin MUs are employed. To evaluate the performance of the digital twin application, a substation simulation model is built on PSCAD/EMTDC simulator, and a single to ground fault detection algorithm for unground distribution is performed on the protection IEDs. Testing results show that the twin application operates properly to generate electrical current and signal and publish sample values (SVs) to the network. Moreover, generic object-oriented substation events (GOOSE) message which is published by protection IEDs is subscribed by circuit breaker management (CBM) and used for controlling circuit breaker model on PSCAD.

articleTitle: Protection Configuration and Circuit Optimization Schemes of 220kV Line Transformer Group
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Currently, the green and low-carbon transformation of electricity is accelerating, and the cumulative installed scale of new energy is constantly expanding. In order to save investment, some 220kV new energy plants adopt line transformer group wiring, and separate circuit breakers protection are required to achieve failure protection function. This article proposes two types of protection configuration and circuit optimization schemes for 220kV line transformer groups. By optimizing the secondary circuit, the circuit by which line protection actions to trip the main transformer is added, and separate circuit breaker protection can no longer be configured. After optimization, it can achieve dual failure protection functions, avoid the risk of no failure protection or dead zone protection caused by improper circuit breaker protection configuration, save investment costs, and reduce equipment operation and maintenance costs, enhance reliability of protection.

articleTitle: Research on Two Stage Zero Sequence Inverse Time Current Protection and Its Setting Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The principle and composition of traditional stage based fixed time zero sequence overcurrent protection are simple, but as the structure of ultra-high voltage power grids becomes more complex, its setting coordination becomes increasingly difficult. The zero sequence inverse time current protection has the characteristic of “larger current, faster action”. When there is a difference in the short-circuit current of adjacent lines, it can naturally achieve selective cooperation between upper and lower lines, and is gradually widely used in backup protection. In existing applications of zero sequence inverse time current protection, a single inverse time curve is used to form zero sequence inverse time current protection. This paper analyzes the widely adopted setting principle of “adopting unified inverse time characteristics and setting value for the entire network” in China, and points out that using a single inverse time curve to form zero sequence inverse time current protection may lead to the problem of long protection action time when high resistance grounding occurs. In response to this issue, this paper proposes a solution to form a zero sequence inverse time current protection using two inverse time curves, and proposes setting methods for each of the two inverse time curves. Theoretical analysis and numerical example verification show that this scheme can effectively improve the speediness of zero sequence inverse time current protection when high resistance grounding occurs, and has certain practical application value.

articleTitle: Fault Analysis of DCSST MV Side Bipolar Short Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Based on DCSST equipment in the flexible medium voltage DC distribution network, this paper analyzes the fault of bipolar short circuit on the medium voltage side at the DCSST outlet from two aspects: control strategy and circuit structure. The dynamic response of control link is analyzed by Laplace transform, and the fault current characteristics in DCSST are analyzed by dynamic circuit method. The analysis shows that the low voltage side does not cause overcurrent due to fault, the fault current in the middle voltage side has two-stage characteristics, and the DCSST itself has the ability to block the fault current. Finally, the rationality and correctness of the analysis are preliminarily verified by PSCAD.

articleTitle: An Online Fault Location Method for DC Distribution Networks Using Adaptive Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Accurate and timely fault location is a crucial technique in the DC distribution network for system stability and power restoration. In this paper, a double-ended fault location method based on parameter estimation using an adaptive Kalman filter is proposed. First, a DC line model considering both line-to-ground and line-to-line faults is established, from which the mathematical relation between line voltage, current and reactor voltage is derived. Then a fault location method based on adaptive Kalman filter algorithm is introduced to estimate the fault parameter. At last the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified in different fault scenarios in a multi-terminal DC distribution network with MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: An Improved Grid-Forming Control Strategy of Energy Storage System for Enhancing Low-Voltage Ride Through Capability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Under the “double carbon” target, the Grid-forming (GFM) storage stations have been used rapidly to stabilize the intermittent and unstable output power from renewable energy resources. However, the recent studies on the control strategies for these storage stations are paying main attention to simulating the synchronous generation characteristics. Once the grid fault occurs, the existing control strategies of the GFM inverter have the overcurrent problems and the inaccurate reactive power supply. In order to solve the above problems, an improved GFM control strategy is proposed in order to enhance the low voltage ride through capability. Under the grid fault the Q-v droop control is deactivated for ensuring the reactive power control accuracy. And the reactive power reference of the virtual synchronous generator control is reset based on the low voltage ride through requirement. Meanwhile, an active power limiter is added into the virtual synchronous generator control in order to limit the current through the inverter. Finally, the tested 10 kW grid-forming energy storage station is built based on PSCAD/EMTDC to verify the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Security Constrained Economic Dispatch Based on Shift Factor Adaptive Calculation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Security-constrained economic dispatch (SCED) is a dispatch plan for generating units that aim to achieve economic efficiency and safety developed by power system control centers. To meet the security and economic requirements of security-constrained economic dispatch, the market operator adjusts transmission line currents to satisfy security constraints and allocates adjusted surpluses or costs to maximize economic benefits when the transmission line load exceeds security constraints during safety verification. The sensitivity of branch currents to the injected power at each bus is defined as the shift factor of network security constraints. The sensitivity relationship between unit outputs and line loads could be derived by calculating the sensitivity coefficient matrix based on the line load direction matrix and the system conductivity matrix. Selecting an appropriate isolated shift factor is challenging yet crucial to achieving safe and constrained economic network operation. This paper analyzes transmission factor selection schemes: coefficient proportional screening and coefficient by screening. By comparing these schemes, the study aims to rationalize the selection of the isolated shift factor and achieve a safe and economically optimized network operation.

articleTitle: Differential Protection Sensitivity Enhancement Scheme for AC Transmission Lines Connecting to VSC-HVDC Station
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the vigorous development of renewable energy and the popularization of HVDC transmission, the structure of power sources has changed a lot. The output current amplitude of power electronic devices is limited, the phase angle of current is controlled, and the characteristics of the sequential component are affected by the converter control strategy, which are different from fault characteristics of SGs. When the AC power system is connected to a large-capacity cross-area VSC-HVDC station, the sensitivity of the conventional current differential protection is reduced during fault on AC transmission line connecting to VSC-HVDC station. To solve the problem of insufficient sensitivity of conventional differential protection on AC transmission line connecting to VSC-HVDC station, this paper analyzed the fault characteristics of AC transmission line connecting to VSC-HVDC station during fault and proposed a current differential protection sensitivity enhancement scheme applicable to AC transmission line connecting to VSC-HVDC station. The scheme can improve the protection performance of the AC transmission line connecting to VSC-HVDC station, supporting the construction of a new type power system.

articleTitle: A Phase-Trajectory-Based Out-of-Step Detection Scheme and its Verification in RTDS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In recent years, with the continuous integration of renewable energy sources and the development of long-distance large-capacity AC/DC transmission lines, the dynamics of the power systems have become more complex, and the safe and stable operation of power grids also faces new challenges. Accurate and rapid determination of power system out-of-step is crucial for the subsequent control and the power system safe and stable operation. However, due to the complexity of power systems, existing transient out-of-step simulation methods are often time-consuming. In this paper, an out-of-step detection scheme based on phase trajectories is proposed. Then it is verified in a real-time digital simulation system (RTDS). By building control modules including the power angle extraction module, real-time grouping module, and the convexity and concavity of the phase trajectory discrimination module, the out-of-step detection is realized. Finally, the tests in RTDS verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Backup Solution for Traveling Wave Differential Protection Under Synchronization Failure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Traveling wave differential protection (TWDP) has shown advantages over traditional current differential protection in terms of sensitivity, rapidity and immunity to distributed capacitive current. However, existing TWDP schemes depends heavily on data synchronization through either GPS or communication, of which the potential failure should be considered. This paper discusses the backup solutions for TWDP in condition of synchronization failure. Firstly, the influence of synchronization error to TWDP is analyzed. The results indicate that such error would lead to mal-operation under external faults. Secondly, a backup algorithm is proposed to handle the synchronization failure issus. Extensive simulation experiments based on the PSCAD/EMTDC software show that the proposed method could avoid mal-operation under external faults while maintain sensitivity to internal faults even if synchronization error is large.

articleTitle: A Novel Control Strategy of Wind-Energy Storage Integrated System to Suppress Wind Power Fluctuation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In recent years, in order to deal with the problems of primary energy shortage and environmental pollution, the installed capacity of wind power has been rising, and the grid-connected scale has been increasing year by year. However, since the randomness and volatility of wind energy are more serious, it is of practical significance to inhibit the wind power fluctuation and reduce its impact on the safe and stable operation of the power grid. This paper proposes a wind - energy storage integrated system of wind turbine innovation model, the use of supercapacitor construction of the energy storage system to suppress the wind power fluctuations, this wind-energy storage integrated system is relatively flexible, can be separate scheduling and control of the generating unit, improve the reliability of the system. On this basis, the charging and discharging strategy of the energy storage system based on sliding average filtering is proposed, which uses the sliding average filtering technology to filter out the high-frequency component in the captured wind power, to obtain the power command of the grid-side converter, and to output the smooth wind power. Secondly, considering the charging state of the supercapacitor, a SOC recovery control strategy is proposed to make secondary corrections to the power commands of the grid-side converter to avoid overcharging and over-discharging of the energy storage system, so as to make the energy storage system operate stably for a long period of time. Finally, a real wind farm is used as an example for simulation analysis, and the simulation results verify the reasonableness and effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Research on Protection Circuit Breaker for Photovoltaic Grid Connection with Collaborative Measurement and Control Design of Photovoltaic Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: A circuit breaker shall be installed at the AC outlet side of the photovoltaic inverter, i.e. the photovoltaic parallel point, as a protection switch, which can monitor and protect the distribution network and the photovoltaic power generation system. Since the equipment connected to the power distribution master station must pass the authenticated encryption chip to encrypt the communication message, the existing data up and down transmission channel of the photovoltaic power generation system through the mobile communication network is difficult to combine with the encryption method of the distribution station area, and it often lacks information interaction and cooperative scheduling with the distribution station area. PDZ879/02 photovoltaic grid connection protection circuit breaker is designed. It integrates photovoltaic protection function, HPLC-LoRa wireless dual-mode communication, power quality monitoring, photovoltaic inverter collaborative measurement and control and other power Internet of things functions. The photovoltaic circuit breaker has a dual MCU design of master-slave architecture. It uses an external RS485 serial port to connect the photovoltaic inverter, and can collect and upload the operation status of the inverter. It adjusts the power generation state of the photovoltaic inverter locally according to the parameters sent by the main station or the station area fusion terminal. The experimental test shows that the photovoltaic circuit breaker can realize various protection functions, and can send the data to the substation fusion terminal and the distribution automation cloud master station, and operate in coordination with the photovoltaic inverter according to the control strategy.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting Analysis and Sensing Application of Cantilever Structure Based on Aeolian Vibration and Piezoelectric Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Based on aeolian vibration and piezoelectric effect, a cantilever energy harvester is proposed to supply energy to a micro-meteorological online monitoring sensing system for transmission lines. According to the Hamiltonian variational principle and Gauss's law, the distributed parameter coupling model of the piezoelectric cantilever energy harvesting module in the system is established, and the theoretical analytical expression of the output response of the energy harvesting module is derived by the Galerkin decomposition method and the force electrolytic coupling method. The influences of external excitation frequency and external load resistance on the output response of the system energy harvesting module are discussed. The results indicate that the highest output power is obtained when the external excitation frequency is equal to the natural frequency of the structure. Besides, the optimal external load resistance is always exciting with maximum electric power and the smallest vibration displacement. Finally, through indoor tests, the practicability of the self-powered micro-meteorological online monitoring system proposed in this paper is demonstrated. The research results in this paper can provide theoretical and experimental reference for the study of self-energy harvesting of transmission line online monitoring systems, and help for the safe operation and risk warning of transmission lines.

articleTitle: Inter-Turn Fault Identification Method of Shunt Reactor Based on RMS Value Characteristics of Inductance in Linear Flux Region
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Taking UHV and UHV shunt reactor as the research object, it is pointed out that the inrush current of shunt reactor without small neutral point reactance will be more serious, which is the main case for the misoperation of turn protection. The current characteristics of shunt reactor with inter-turn fault are analyzed. It is pointed out that the characteristic relationship between the RMS value of inductance and the rated inductance in the phase current linear region changes after inter-turn fault occurs. Based on the characteristic relationship between the root mean square value of inductance and the rated inductance at each time in the phase current linear region, combined with the sampling peak spacing before and after the differential phase current zero crossing and the deviation degree of peak spacing before and after the phase current zero crossing under the power frequency characteristics, the reactor inter-turn fault and the no-load closing saturation are identified. If the reactor inter-turn fault is identified, the turn protection is opened by short delay. Inter-turn protection is blocked if the no-load closing saturation is identified. Simulation results verify the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: PV Injection Power Estimation Method Based on Voltage Sensitivity Analysis Optimized by SA-BPSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The on-grid status and output power of grid-connected photovoltaics have important impact on the safe and economic operation of the distribution network. However, in many cases, distribution system operators are unable to directly and accurately monitor the PV's operating status. To address these problems, this paper proposes a PV injection power estimation method based on voltage sensitivity analysis optimized by adaptive Simulated Annealing-Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (SA-BPSO) algorithm. Firstly, the voltage sensitivity matrix is constructed based on the relationship between node injection power and node voltage magnitude. Secondly, an adaptive SA-BPSO algorithm is utilized to determine the minimum number and optimal locations of voltage monitoring devices. Subsequently, the observable voltage magnitude data are jointly calculated with the voltage sensitivity matrix to estimate the PV injection power. Finally, the proposed method is tested using the IEEE 34-node distribution network. The results show that the proposed method can accurately estimate the PV on-grid status and power output for the three validation scenarios, namely, PV off-grid, PV power variation, and the combination of the two. It can serve as a guideline for achieving accurate PV injection power estimation with as few voltage monitoring devices as possible under the requirement of meeting the economic constraints of voltage monitoring devices.

articleTitle: Research on Coordinated Control Strategy for AC Fault Ride-Through of Wind-Solar-Thermal-Storage Combined Flexible-Direct Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: When the AC grid connected to the multi-terminal flexible DC transmission system fails, the voltage of the common connection point of the system drops and the current rises, resulting in the reduction of the output power capacity of the receiving-end converter station and the generation of unbalanced power on the DC line. The unbalanced power causes the DC system voltage to deviate from the rated voltage, which may cause the converter station to be disconnected in severe cases. Therefore, based on the Modular Multilevel Converter control strategy, an AC fault ride-through coordinated control strategy considering the combination of energy consumption and energy storage is proposed. According to the working mode of the energy storage system during normal operation, the working mode of the energy storage system after the fault is analyzed and studied: According to the characteristics that the resistance of the energy dissipation resistor is inversely proportional to the active power consumption, the traditional energy dissipation resistor topology is improved, and the coordination of energy storage and energy consumption is studied. At the same time, the fault characteristics of the fault current sequence component under the control strategy and the influence of the transition resistance on it are further analyzed. The results show that the negative sequence current on the flexible side of the fault line can be suppressed when an asymmetric short-circuit fault occurs. When the AC grid-connected point voltage drops to 0.9p.u., the converter station prioritizes the generation of reactive power; When the AC system at the receiving-end fails, the DC system will also have a transient response. For example, the DC system generates unbalanced power accumulation and the DC overvoltage phenomenon occurs. The unbalanced power generated will be preferentially consumed within the loop network. Therefore, only the three-phase short circuit will cause the DC voltage to exceed 1.05p.u. At this time, the DC system is put into the energy dissipation circuit, which consumes the unbalanced active power of the system and stabilizes the DC voltage in the range of 1.0 ~ 1.05p.u. . By controlling the energy storage system to absorb active power, the active power output of the sending converter station is reduced, and Energy dissipation circuit cooperates with energy storage system to reduce energy waste. Finally, the effectiveness of the coordinated control strategy of hardware and software is verified by RTDS simulation experiments, and the consistency between the fault characteristics and theoretical analysis under this scheme is confirmed.

articleTitle: Energy Storage Planning Method to Improve the Resiliency of Distribution Network Under Disaster Weather
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: At present, the energy storage configuration in the distribution network usually considers economic factors such as loss reduction and arbitrage, and less considers the use of energy storage to improve the safe operation of the distribution network in disaster weather, and the energy storage configuration planning needs comprehensive optimization. In this paper, an energy storage planning method is proposed to improve the resiliency of the distribution network under severe weather conditions. With the access point, capacity and operation mode of the energy storage device under different weather scenarios as the decision variables, and the lowest investment and operation cost of the distribution network as the objective function, a mixed integer programming model of energy storage configuration is constructed. An example of IEEE-33 node system is taken to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method. This approach enables the energy storage to flexibly respond to different operation scenarios of the distribution network, and maximize its potential to participate in the safe and economic operation of the distribution network in normal, severe and extreme weather.

articleTitle: Modified Isolated Modular Multilevel Converter for Bipolar DC Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The Bipolar Low-voltage DC distribution system has the advantages of flexible load connection and high operational reliability. The Isolated Modular Multilevel DC/DC Converter (IMMDC) is an attractive solution for interconnecting medium voltage DC (MVDC) grids with low voltage DC (LVDC) grids. With a modular multilevel converter (MMC) on the MVDC side and a full-bridge (FB) or a half-bridge (HB) on the LVDC side, the IMMDC can be flexibly extended to different voltages and power ratings. However, existing IMMDC topologies are limited to two-port operation where the full-bridge DC voltage and power must always remain the same. This paper presents a modified IMMDC for interconnecting MVDC grids and bipolar LVDC grids. The mathematical model and equivalent circuit of the proposed modified IMMDC are derived. Then the power flow under balanced/unbalanced power transfer and the operation of a single pole short circuit fault on the bipolar LVDC grids are considered. At the same time, a control scheme for this converter under different operating conditions is proposed. Finally, MATLAB/ Simulink simulation results are presented to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed modified IMMDC.

articleTitle: Reactive Power Optimization Control Strategy of AC Weak Grid Considering Small Hydro-Power Access
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of voltage fluctuations in distribution network and power quality caused by the large-scale access of small hydro-power under weak grid conditions, a reactive power optimization control strategy was proposed. Based on the analysis of the operating characteristics of small hydro-power, especially the voltage characteristics, a multi-objective reactive power control model of distribution network of small hydro-power was established. Combined with the improved Bat-Algorithm, to avoid the algorithm falling into local optimization, probabilistic elite pool disturbance strategy was introduced, by setting up the external storage device and using the phasing-out mechanism to sort the crowded distance of the calculated target value, and the Pareto optimal solution set of the model was finally obtained. Through the application of IEEE33 node system for simulation, test results show that the optimization control strategy can effectively solve the problems of network loss optimization and voltage fluctuations. The proposed method has theoretical and practical significance for the control operation of distribution networks containing distributed small hydro-power.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of MESS in Distribution Network Fault Recovery by Considering the Impulse of Loop Closing Current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the network configuration generated after distribution network fault does not consider current impulses and out-of-limit during loop closing, this paper utilizes the idea of active participation of distributed power sources in control to suppress loop closing impulse current. To improve the safety and reliability of the distribution network fault recovery process, a strategy of utilizing the flexibility of mobile energy storage system (MESS) to assist in closing loop of the distribution network is proposed. Firstly, the spatiotemporal cost of MESS participation in scheduling is analyzed, as well as the impact of the distance between MESS and the closing point on the impulse current. Then, with the goal of suppressing loop closing impulse current, maximizing load recovery rate, and minimizing MESS scheduling cost, a model of MESS participating in network reconfiguration scheduling is constructed. By determining the node location of MESS and power regulation reference values during the distribution network fault recovery process, the proposed model forms a MESS scheduling and control basic sequence of “reconfiguration scheme generation-energy storage movement-energy storage power regulation-loop closing”. Finally, the IEEE 33-node system is adopted to verify the effectiveness of MESS in suppressing current impulse during the process of loop closing. The results show that the proposed method can enhance the feasibility of network reconfiguration schemes and improve the resilience of distribution network.

articleTitle: The New Principle of New Power System Line Transient Protection Based on Time-Frequency Catastrophe Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The introduction of power electronic converters has changed the fault characteristics of the traditional power grid. It is difficult for traditional differential protection to meet the protection needs, prone to sensitivity reduction or even the risk of rejection, when the AC line fault occurs. To solve this problem, an AC line protection principle based on the fault full current multi-order mutation was proposed. The protection is based on the regular changes in the waveform deformation characteristics and mutation characteristics of the line on both sides after the fault occurs. Extracting mutation eigenvalues of full current signals on both sides by matrix gradient algorithm. That is the mutation degree of the full current signal on both sides is described. In turn, the longitudinal protection is constructed. The proposed method does not need to extract the power frequency characteristics compared with the traditional fast protection of transient quantities, Solve the problem that the fixed transient quantities cannot be accurately extracted by using the periodic component algorithm under the controlled short-circuit current, and considering the influence of the control strategy of the flexible converter on the protection principle, the protection speed and sensitivity are effectively improved. Finally, the simulation model of the converter grid-connected system is built in PSCAD/EMTDC and the effectiveness of the protection is verified. The proposed protection fault identification time is less than 7.5ms. The proposed protection can better meet the demand of the converter grid-connected line for protection speed and selectivity.

articleTitle: Pilot Protection Scheme for Collection Line of All-DC Offshore Wind Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: To adapt to the development of long-distance offshore wind power, the all-DC transmission system based on DC collection and DC transmission has emerged. However, due to the addition of power electronic components and the influence of weak boundary characteristics of transmission lines, new requirements have been put forward for relay protection. The paper firstly proposes a topology structure of the all-DC system and analyses its fault characteristics. Then, a pilot protection method of collection line based on Kendall correlation coefficient is proposed for the given topology. This method utilizes the current correlation at both terminals of the line to select the faulty zone and faulty pole simultaneously. Finally, the performance of the proposed protection scheme is verified on the MATLAB/SIMULINK platform, and the results show that under different fault conditions, the selection of the faulty area and faulty pole can be reliably completed under a sampling window length of 1.2ms, meeting the rapidity requirements of all-DC system. It can withstand 20dB of noise interference and a certain transition resistance, and has advantages on its simple algorithm and low sampling frequency requirements.

articleTitle: Graph-Based Automatic Identification and Correction of Bus Topology in 500kV Substations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Under the digital transformation of power systems, there is a growing demand for intelligent power grid analysis. This requires automatic and precise batch modeling over massive power equipment with standardized topology and measurement data entry. However, due to limitations in data management, power grid companies usually have errors and non-standardized naming of topological data. This work introduces a graph database to construct a semi-realtime topology data governance method. It considers semantic recognition, isolated electrical component verification, quantified relationships between electrical components, and power system operation regulations as constraints to perform automatic identification and correction of bus topology structure in substations. The method comprises a data identification module and an error data correction module to achieve automatic generation and intelligent analysis of substation topology. While a relational database relies on complex joins on data tables to process data, a graph database can efficiently perform batch synchronous parallel calculations. The method adopts a graph database instead of the commonly used relational database. The minimum grain of the data system is extended from discrete numbers to nodes and edges in the graph. The method validation section determines the 500kV-side bus topology structure through quantitative analysis of the topological data. Such a method adapts well to the development trend of the Internet and meets the needs of large-scale multi-dimensional cross-system real-time queries of the power automation analysis business.

Author Keywords: quantitative relationship of bus connection type

articleTitle: Research on Relay Protection of 10kV Distribution Network Considering the Operating Characteristics of Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: A virtual power plant aggregates many distributed resources. Its operation mode is complex and changeable. The distribution network with virtual power plants has great differences in power flow distribution under different operation modes, and the short-circuit current flowing through local relays changes frequently. It is difficult for traditional relay protection to adapt. Therefore, this paper first models the inverter interface distributed generation (IIDG) aggregated by virtual power plants. Then the phase difference between the fault component of the positive sequence voltage of the bus and the fault component of the positive sequence current of each feeder is used to construct a protection scheme. This scheme is not affected by the operation mode of the virtual power plant and can be accurately located under various fault conditions. Finally, a simulation example is built using PSCAD to verify the above method.

articleTitle: Adaptability Analysis of Directional Element for Inverter Interfaced System Considering Fault Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Due to the fragility of power electronic devices and controllability of grid-connected inverters, photovoltaic power plants change the fault current characteristics of transmission lines, resulting in adaptability problems for various directional relays based on traditional synchronous power supply fault characteristics. In this paper, the phase Angle variation of the side sequence impedance of a photovoltaic power station is deduced by considering the control objective of negative sequence suppression. Its influence on the directional element based on the sequence component is analyzed. Set up a photovoltaic power station in the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation platform, test and verify sequence impedance Angle changes on the traditional direction element adaptive problems.

articleTitle: A Method for Locating Latent Faults in Medium Voltage Cables Based on the Traveling Wave Dual Terminal Principle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The role of cables in urban medium voltage distribution networks is crucial. Fault location based on detecting potential cable faults is of great significance for preventing permanent cable faults and ensuring the safe operation of the power system. This article proposes a dual terminal traveling wave fault location method for latent faults in medium voltage distribution cables based on wavelet packet transform and correlation analysis. Firstly, use wavelet packet transform to process the cable fault signal, extract the fault feature signal, and determine the accurate time when the fault traveling wave reaches the two ends of the cable. Secondly, use correlation analysis to determine the time difference At between the arrival of fault traveling waves at both ends. Based on the general high-frequency traveling wave velocity and traveling wave ranging formula, the fault is located, and the effectiveness of the proposed dual terminal traveling wave ranging method for latent faults is verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Stochastic Optimal Allocation of Photovoltaic and Storage Capacity in Distribution System for New Energy Accommodation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: To actively promote the low-carbon transformation of energy, constructing a new power system with new energy as the main body has received widespread attention. And the optimal allocation of the photovoltaic and storage capacity for the distribution network is the basis for ensuring the economical and safe operation of the power system. Considering the uncertainty of photovoltaic power output, a two-stage multi-objective stochastic optimization model is constructed to allocate and operate photovoltaic and storage capacity for the distribution system connected to renewable energy sources. First, a two-stage multi-objective stochastic optimization model for planning and operation is established by considering system investment and operation costs, photovoltaic curtailment penalty costs, network loss costs, and voltage offset targets. In addition, considering the uncertainty of photovoltaic output, multiple scenarios are used to characterize the uncertainty of photovoltaic output, combined with the K-means clustering method for scenario reduction. Particle swarm algorithms are utilized to figure out a two-stage multi-objective model for the planning and operation of photovoltaic and storage systems, employing the IEEE 33 node as an example. The results of this study demonstrate that the optimal allocation of photovoltaic and storage capacity of the distribution system can effectively promote the accommodation of new energy and the construction of a low-carbon energy system.

articleTitle: Research on Single-Ended Protection for Wind Power Full-DC Transmission System Based on Generalized S Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Wind power Full-DC transmission system can effectively solve the problems of harmonic and reactive power compensation that exist in wind power AC collection and transmission, and has broad development prospects. It contains a large number of power electronic converters. These power electronic converters have a limited ability to withstand overcurrent. Therefore, researching fast and accurate fault identification line protection is an urgent need for the development of DC power grids. This article analyzes the attenuation characteristics of the initial traveling wave frequency component at the installation site of internal and external fault. Since the difference in attenuation of the initial traveling wave frequency component of internal and external faults. The paper proposes a single terminal protection based on the high and low-frequency ratio of initial voltage backward traveling wave. Finally, a four-terminal wind power full-DC transmission system model is established and verified using PSCAD/EMTDC. Theoretical analysis and simulation results show that the proposed protection scheme can correctly internal and external faults, accurately select fault poles, setting is simple and easy to operate, with strong resistance to fault resistance.

articleTitle: Improvement on Hausdorff Distance and its Application to the Backup Protection Scheme for Hybrid HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The hybrid HVDC transmission system applying LCC converter as the rectifier, and MMC converter as the inverter combines the advantages of both types of converter, which makes the protection scheme more complicated. A new pilot protection scheme for the three-terminal hybrid DC transmission system applying energy functions is proposed. The energy function for the LCC converter is extended to be applied in MMC converter to derive the energy level of the hybrid system. Furthermore, an improved Hausdorff distance calculation method is proposed to detect the difference in energy levels between normal and abnormal states. The Hausdorff distances and the floating thresholds are calculated to determine the fault pole and the fault line. Finally, the proposed protection scheme is verified by using the simulation model of Wudongde ±800kV three-terminal hybrid HVDC transmission project and compared with the results derived by the absolute distance method. The results show that the proposed scheme in this paper can identify and trip the fault lines quickly and effectively. It also shows that the proposed scheme can avoid the misoperation caused by abnormal data and ineffectiveness caused by high-resistance ground fault up to 600Ω, which improves the practical application value to some extent.

articleTitle: A Health Status Evaluation Method for Gateway Device Based on Chip-Board-Device Information and Fuzzy Synthesis Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The gateway is an important secondary device in a substation, and its health status can provide guidance for equipment condition maintenance and fault disposal, which is essential to ensure the safe and stable operation of the substation. However, the existing secondary equipment assessment focuses on device or board-level information and lacks an overall consideration of chip-board-device. This paper establishes a three-level device health evaluation system of chip-board-device covering the core boards of the gateway device and proposes a fuzzy comprehensive rating method. In detail, firstly, the typical structure of a gateway device is introduced. Secondly, a three-level equipment health evaluation system of chip-board-device is established. Thirdly, based on fuzzy theory, a comprehensive evaluation method of variable weight gateway device based on deterioration degree correction is given. Finally, the evaluation results under the three weights are compared with examples, and the optimal weight processing method is selected.

articleTitle: A Thyristor-Controlled Superconducting Current Limiting Module on Mitigation of Commutation Failure in LCC-Based HVDC Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With more applications and larger transmission capacity of LCC-HVDC transmission systems, commutation failure has attracted more attention. In view of this problem, existing methods pay less attention to commutation failures caused by severe short-circuit faults on AC or DC side. In this paper a thyristor-controlled superconducting current limiting module is proposed based on resistive superconducting current limiting units. The operating principles are presented followed by detailed analysis for commutation under AC short-circuit faults and DC short-circuit faults. The performance of the proposed method is validated by simulation results in MATLAB/Simulink. The simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively prevent the first commutation failure caused by severe short circuit fault.

articleTitle: Control Parameters Optimization for MMC-HVDC Transmission System with New Energy Weak AC Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The high proportion of new energy and power electronic equipment in the power system presents significant challenges to its stability. In new power systems, large-scale new energy is transmitted via MMC-HVDC through AC collection. The adaptability of converters to weak AC grids has been a growing concern in recent years. The selection of appropriate control parameters is crucial for ensuring stable, efficient, and reliable operation of the DC system. Therefore, this paper aims to study the modeling method of the state space model of MMC-HVDC and the AC new energy system against the background of the new energy weak AC grid. It constructs the small disturbance model of the MMC-HVDC transmission system of the new energy weak AC grid. For the new energy weak AC grid, the new energy power station is simplified as a single-ended MMC-HVDC system with fixed PQ control. The constant voltage source is connected in series with impedance to simulate the strength of the AC system in the AC grid. The MMC-HVDC electric power transmission uses a combination of conventional control strategies to model. The converter station adopts a true bipolar structure, where the positive and negative poles are equipped with DC reactors, and the converter valve adopts a full and half bridge hybrid structure. Additionally, considering the internal dynamic characteristics of the converter, such as the capacitance voltage fluctuation of the converter module, internal circulating arm currents, and internal circulating arm currents suppression controller, a detailed small disturbance model is built. The oscillation mode of the system is obtained through the state space matrix in the small disturbance model, and the main participating factors are calculated and screened out. To clarify the range of control parameter values that can maintain stability in the system, the control parameters are traversed, and the root trajectory of the state space matrix is solved. The stable state of the system is determined, and the feasible region of the control parameters that have a significant impact on the system is calculated and drawn. To obtain better control parameters of the whole system, the control parameter optimization model of multi-terminal MMC-HVDC electric power transmission is constructed based on the particle swarm optimization algorithm, the real eigenvalues, and the damping ratio of oscillation mode. Finally, this article uses PSCAD/EMTDC to construct an electromagnetic transient simulation model for the MMC-HVDC transmission system of the new energy weak AC grid and verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that the proposed parameter optimization method can achieve better dynamic response characteristics of the control system.

Author Keywords: new energy transmission via MMC-HVDC through AC collection

articleTitle: Energy Storage Planning and Configuration of Active Distribution Network Based on Load Ordered Clustering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In order to fully excavate scheduling, periodic characteristics of power load, raise the reliability and economy of the energy storage and distribution network planning, based on the year of the three typical load curves, on the basis of similarity analysis, through the orderly clustering analysis. distribution network planning, based on the year of the three typical load curves, on the basis of similarity analysis, through the orderly clustering method for all kinds of load curves according to the time series of annual finer clustering, and the time series of annual finer clustering. method for all kinds of load curves according to the time series of annual finer clustering, The minimum time unit of dynamic configuration of mobile The minimum time unit of dynamic configuration of mobile energy storage in distribution network is planned according to month, and a method of energy storage planning and configuration of active distribution network based on load ordered clustering. The minimum time unit of dynamic configuration of mobile energy storage in distribution network is planned according to month, and a method of energy storage planning and configuration of active distribution network based on load ordered clustering is proposed. Finally, IEEE33 node system is adopted to verify the proposed scheme. The calculation results show that the energy storage configuration scheme considering the actual time sequence characteristics of the load is more economical and can reflect the actual operation of the distribution network. The calculation results show that the energy storage configuration scheme considering the actual time sequence characteristics of the load is more economical and can reflect the actual operation of the distribution network. The scheme is an effective extension of the flexible use of energy storage equipment in the distribution network, and can better serve the variable operation of active distribution network load, so as to better play the role of energy storage.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control Strategy for Stable Power Transmission of DWPT System Based on Mutual Inductance Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) system has the problem of unstable transmission power caused by the change of coupling coefficient in the process of power transmission. This paper proposes a finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) strategy based on mutual parameter identification for dynamic wireless power transfer system. The transmission characteristics of DWPT system with LCC-S resonant compensation topology is analyzed, and the output current of the inverter in the primary side is taken as reference for mutual inductance identification by particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. Then, the FCS-MPC algorithm based on PSO is used to control the output voltage by changing phase-shift angle in the primary side. For precise control, the compensation calculation of the phase-shift angle is added. The simulation at the end of the paper verifies the accuracy of the PSO algorithm and the effects of proposed strategy under different coupling coefficients and load. The results indicate that the proposed strategy has fast transient response and stable power transmission in DWPT system which can be used to improve the system performance.

Author Keywords: finite control set model predictive control

articleTitle: Research on Health Status Evaluation of Measurement and Control Devices by Fusing Chip-Board-Device Information
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Measurement and control devices are important secondary equipment in substations, and their health status can provide guidance for equipment condition maintenance and troubleshooting, and it is crucial to ensure the health of devices for safe and stable operation of substations. However, the existing secondary equipment assessment focuses on equipment or board-level information and lacks an overall consideration of chip-board-device. This paper establishes a chip-board-complete three-level device health evaluation system covering the core modules of the measurement and control device and proposes a fuzzy comprehensive rating method. Specifically, it is as follows: firstly, the typical structure of the measurement and control device is introduced; secondly, the three-level equipment health evaluation system of the measurement and control device incorporating chip-board-complete machine information is given; again, based on the normal-type affiliation function, the fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method of the measurement and control device is given; finally, the effectiveness of the method is verified by combining with examples.

articleTitle: A Novel Inverter Topology on Mitigation of Commutation Failure in LCC-Based HVDC Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With more applications and larger transmission capacity of LCC-HVDC transmission systems, commutation failure has attracted more attention. In view of this problem, existing methods pay less attention to commutation failures caused by severe short-circuit faults on AC or DC side. Thus an auxiliary method is needed as a supplement. This paper develops a method for SFCLs to suppress commutation failure in HVDC transmission system. A strategy based on SFCLs is designed as an auxiliary method to mitigate commutation failures caused by severe short-circuit faults. The proposed method is based on the proposed module. The operating principles are presented. The performance of the proposed method is validated by simulation results in PSCAD. The simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively prevent the first commutation failure caused by severe short circuit fault.

articleTitle: Synchronization Damping of Grid-forming Converter under DC Voltage/Frequency Mapping Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the integration of a high penetration of new energy sources and power electronic devices, the electrical power system exhibits characteristics of low inertia and weak damping, leading to the emergence of new stability issues. The commonly employed approach to address this issue is virtual synchronous generator control. There exists an analogical relationship between the DC capacitor voltage of the inverter and the rotor speed of the synchronous machine. By normalizing the direct current voltage and utilizing it as the modulation voltage vector's real-time rotational speed, it is possible to induce inertia characteristics in the grid-connected inverter. However, due to the absence of the damping torque like synchronous generators have, which is generated by the mutual interactions between windings that can, alter the induced electromotive force and consequently the electromagnetic power, the synchronous stability of grid-connected inverters under such control is difficult to ensure. Prolonged oscillations with extended durations are prone to occur following disturbances. In response to this challenge, this study initially establishes a small-signal model for grid-connected inverters under this control scheme, confirming the presence of weak damping characteristics. Subsequently, two control strategies are proposed: a droop control scheme for the generator-side inverters, and a virtual power system stabilizer control scheme for the grid-side inverter, aimed at enhancing its damping characteristics. The effectiveness of these two control schemes is validated through small-signal model root locus analysis and simulations using PowerFactory software.

articleTitle: Design of Automatic Identification System for Substation Monitoring Interface Based on Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Substation is one of the key nodes in building a new energy system. The level of intelligence in substations directly affects the safety and efficiency of smart grids. In order to test and evaluate the working status of the substation monitoring interface, this work designs an automatic identification system based on machine vision. Firstly, an intelligent monitoring software and hardware platform for the substation monitoring interface is designed, utilizing a modular approach to decompose subsystems. At the same time, an intelligent entity recognition algorithm based on machine vision is proposed to accurately classify and recognize interface entities, and to compare and verify with test inputs. This system avoids manual verification and comparison, and achieves fully automatic testing of substation monitoring.

articleTitle: Study on Single-Phase Grounding Current Protection of Distribution Line in Neutral Grounding System via arc Suppression Coil
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
